topics.title: Gotchas
topics.content_html:
# Mutable default — shared across calls
def append(item, bucket=[]):   # BAD
    bucket.append(item); return bucket

def append(item, bucket=None):  # GOOD
    if bucket is None: bucket = []
    bucket.append(item); return bucket

# is vs ==
a is b          # identity
a == b          # equality

# Late-binding closures
funcs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
funcs[0]()      # 2 — all see final i
funcs = [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)]  # capture

# Generator exhaustion
g = (x*x for x in range(3))
list(g); list(g)  # second is []

# Prefer specific exceptions over bare except
Common mistake Mutable defaults and late-binding closures are classic traps. Prefer None defaults and default-arg capture in lambdas.

topics.title: Ownership & Borrowing
topics.content_html:
Every value has one owner. Non-Copy assignment moves; the old binding is invalid.

let s1 = String::from("hello");
let s2 = s1;                  // move — s1 invalid
println!("{s2}");

let n1 = 5;                   // i32 is Copy
let n2 = n1;                  // both valid

fn print_len(s: &String) -> usize { s.len() }
print_len(&s);                // borrow, s still valid

fn add_world(s: &mut String) { s.push_str(", world"); }
let mut s = String::from("hello");
add_world(&mut s);

// either one &mut OR any number of & — never both
let s3 = s2.clone();
★ Ownership defaults Prefer borrowing (&T / &mut T) over cloning. Own with T only when you need exclusive ownership.
Need ownership? │ ├─ no -> borrow │ ├─ read-only -> &T │ └─ mutate -> &mut T └─ yes -> move T └─ shared ownership? -> Arc<T> (or Rc<T> single-threaded)
Common mistake Don't clone() just to silence the borrow checker — prefer a borrow or a redesign.

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.content_html:
No exceptions. Recoverable: Result<T, E>. Unrecoverable: panic!.

fn divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String> {
    if b == 0.0 { return Err("Cannot divide by zero!".into()); }
    Ok(a / b)
}

match divide(10.0, 0.0) {
    Ok(r) => println!("Result: {r}"),
    Err(e) => println!("{e}"),
}

fn read_number() -> Result<i32, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("num.txt")?;
    let n: i32 = s.trim().parse()?;
    Ok(n)
}

result.unwrap_or(0);
Some(4).map(|n| n * 2);

topics.title: Gotchas
topics.content_html:
// Unnecessary clone — prefer a borrow
let s2 = s1.clone();   // only when you need ownership

// Borrowing across mutation
let r = &v[0];
v.push(1);             // error while r lives

// unwrap in libraries
value.unwrap();        // prefer ? / unwrap_or / ok_or

// Blocking inside async
std::thread::sleep(...);  // use tokio::time::sleep

// Mutex poisoning — a panic while holding the lock poisons it;
// later .lock() calls return Err instead of panicking silently
let guard = match mutex.lock() {
    Ok(g) => g,
    Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner(), // recover the data anyway
};

// Prefer &T / &mut T; Arc only for shared ownership across threads
Common mistake clone() and unwrap() silence the compiler but hide design issues. Prefer borrows and ? propagation.

const limit = 10;   // the binding cannot be reassigned
let total = 0;      // block scoped, can be reassigned
var legacy = 1;     // function scoped; avoid in new code

const user = { name: "Ada" };
user.name = "Grace";   // allowed: const protects the binding, not the object
Object.freeze(user);   // shallow freeze: properties can no longer change

// let and const are not usable before their declaration runs
// console.log(later);  // ReferenceError (temporal dead zone)
let later = 1;

// var is hoisted and starts as undefined
console.log(typeof hoisted);  // "undefined"
var hoisted = 1;

for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  setTimeout(() => console.log(i), 0);  // 0, 1, 2
}
★ Default Start with const, switch to let only when the variable is reassigned, and leave var to legacy code.

topics.title: Classes
topics.content_html:
class Account {
  #balance = 0;                // private field
  static count = 0;

  constructor(owner) {
    this.owner = owner;
    Account.count++;
  }

  get balance() { return this.#balance; }

  deposit(amount) {
    if (amount <= 0) throw new RangeError("amount must be positive");
    this.#balance += amount;
    return this;
  }

  static from(data) { return new Account(data.owner); }

  #audit() { return `${this.owner}: ${this.#balance}`; }
  toString() { return this.#audit(); }
}

class Savings extends Account {
  constructor(owner, rate) {
    super(owner);              // must run before using this
    this.rate = rate;
  }
}

const a = new Account("Ada").deposit(50);
a.balance;                     // 50
a instanceof Account;          // true
★ Default Keep state private with #fields, and expose it through getters and methods.
When to use Use a class when several objects share behavior and state. A plain object plus functions is simpler when they do not.
Common mistake Calling a class without new throws a TypeError. A class declaration cannot be used before the line that defines it.

topics.title: Iteration & Iterators
topics.content_html:
for (const x of [1, 2, 3]) {}
for (const [i, x] of ["a", "b"].entries()) {}

function* range(start, end) {
  for (let i = start; i < end; i++) yield i;
}
[...range(0, 3)];                 // [0, 1, 2]

class Countdown {
  constructor(from) { this.from = from; }
  *[Symbol.iterator]() {
    for (let i = this.from; i > 0; i--) yield i;
  }
}
[...new Countdown(3)];            // [3, 2, 1]

const it = [10, 20][Symbol.iterator]();
it.next();                        // { value: 10, done: false }

// Iterator helpers (ES2025): lazy, one value at a time
range(0, Infinity)
  .filter((n) => n % 2 === 0)
  .map((n) => n * n)
  .take(3)
  .toArray();                     // [0, 4, 16]

// Async iteration
for await (const chunk of stream) {}

Common mistake An iterator can only be consumed once. Spreading a generator twice gives an empty second result.

topics.title: Async & Await
topics.content_html:
async function load(url) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(url);      // fetch is a host API
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
    return await response.json();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("load failed", error);
    throw error;
  }
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Parallel instead of one after another
const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([load("/users"), load("/posts")]);

await Promise.allSettled(tasks);       // every outcome, never rejects
await Promise.race([task(), sleep(1000)]);
await Promise.any([mirrorA(), mirrorB()]);   // first success

const { promise, resolve, reject } = Promise.withResolvers();

const controller = new AbortController();  // host API for cancelling
fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal });
controller.abort();
★ Default Start independent work together and await the group with Promise.all(), instead of awaiting one call after another.
Common mistake array.forEach(async ...) does not wait for the promises it creates. Use for...of with await, or Promise.all(array.map(...)). A promise that rejects with nobody handling it is reported as an unhandled rejection.

try {
  risky();
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TypeError) {
    recover();
  } else {
    throw error;                  // do not swallow what you cannot handle

} finally {

}

class ValidationError extends Error {
  constructor(message, options) {
    super(message, options);
    this.name = "ValidationError";
  }
}

try {
  parse(input);
} catch (cause) {
  throw new ValidationError("Invalid input", { cause });   // keep the original error

features.summary: arguments.callee refers to the function that is currently running, from inside that function.

ecmascript.note: Accessing arguments.callee throws a TypeError in strict-mode functions.

migration.note: Give the function expression a name and call it by that name.

features.title: Legacy octal literals
features.summary: Integer literals written with a leading zero, such as 0755, and octal escape sequences in strings.

ecmascript.note: Described in the compatibility annex (Annex B) rather than the core grammar.
Legacy octal literals and octal escape sequences are a SyntaxError in strict mode.

migration.note: Use the 0o prefix (ES2015).

features.title: String.prototype.substr()
features.summary: Extracts part of a string using a start index and a length.

ecmascript.note: New in the compatibility annex (Annex B), which first appeared in ES3. Not part of the core language.
Legacy feature kept for web compatibility (Annex B). Prefer slice() or substring(). It is not scheduled for removal.

migration.note: substr takes (start, length); slice takes (start, end).

features.title: escape() and unescape()
features.summary: Global functions that apply a percent-style encoding to strings.

ecmascript.note: Part of the core language in the earliest editions. Moved to the compatibility annex (Annex B) in ES3.
Legacy functions kept for web compatibility (Annex B). They use a non-standard %uXXXX form for characters above U+00FF. Use encodeURIComponent() and decodeURIComponent().

migration.note: Results differ for non-ASCII characters and for characters such as +, / and @.

features.title: encodeURI() and encodeURIComponent()
features.summary: Functions that encode and decode strings for use inside URIs.

features.title: for...in enumeration
features.summary: for...in loops over an object's enumerable string keys, including inherited ones.

ecmascript.note: The order is now partly specified. For ordinary objects, own keys come first (integer indices in ascending order, then string keys in the order they were added), followed by inherited keys. Proxies and other exotic objects, and objects changed during the loop, can still differ.

features.title: Strict mode
features.summary: The 'use strict' directive switches code to a restricted variant of the language with more errors.

ecmascript.note: Class bodies and module code are always strict, with no directive needed.

features.title: JSON.parse() and JSON.stringify()
features.summary: A built-in JSON object for parsing and producing JSON text.

ecmascript.note: JSON.stringify now escapes lone surrogates so its output is always well-formed, and U+2028 and U+2029 are allowed inside string literals.

node.note: JSON.stringify returns well-formed output and string literals may contain U+2028 and U+2029.

migration.note: eval runs arbitrary code; JSON.parse only parses data.

features.title: Array iteration methods
features.summary: forEach, map, filter, reduce, reduceRight, some, every, indexOf and lastIndexOf on arrays.

features.title: Function.prototype.bind()
features.summary: Returns a function with a fixed this value and optional leading arguments.

features.title: let and const
features.summary: Block-scoped variable declarations, with const for bindings that are never reassigned.

migration.note: var is function-scoped, so every callback sees the final i (3). let creates a new binding per iteration (0, 1, 2).

features.title: Arrow functions
features.summary: Compact function syntax whose this is taken from the surrounding code.

migration.note: Arrow functions have no own this, arguments or prototype, so they cannot replace every function expression.

features.title: Classes
features.summary: class declarations with constructors, methods, extends and super.

ecmascript.note: Class bodies gained public and private fields, private methods and static initialization blocks.

migration.note: A class must be called with new, and class declarations are not usable before their line runs.

features.title: Template literals
features.summary: Backtick strings with ${expression} interpolation, multi-line text and tagged templates.

ecmascript.note: Tagged templates may contain invalid escape sequences; their cooked value is undefined instead of a SyntaxError.

node.note: Tagged templates accept invalid escape sequences.

migration.legacy: var message = "Hello, " + name + "! You have " + count + " messages.";

features.title: Destructuring
features.summary: Pattern syntax that unpacks arrays and objects into variables.

migration.legacy:
var host = options.host;
var port = options.port;

features.title: Default, rest and spread parameters
features.summary: Default parameter values, rest parameters, and spread in calls and array literals.

migration.note: A default applies only when the argument is undefined. The || pattern also replaces 0, empty strings and false.

features.title: ES modules
features.summary: import and export statements for native modules.

node.note: ES modules need a .mjs file name, or "type": "module" in the nearest package.json. Earlier releases that supported it: 12.17.0 to 12.19.0.

features.title: Promises
features.summary: Promise objects for asynchronous results, with then, catch, Promise.all and Promise.race.

migration.note: The functions must return promises. Wrap callback-style APIs with new Promise.

features.title: Binary and octal literals
features.summary: 0b and 0o prefixes for binary and octal integer literals.

features.title: includes(), startsWith(), endsWith() and repeat()
features.summary: String methods for testing whether text contains, starts with or ends with another string, and for repeating a string.

features.title: Object.assign()
features.summary: Copies own enumerable properties from one or more objects onto a target object.

migration.note: Object.assign also copies symbol-keyed properties and runs setters on the target.

features.title: Array.prototype.includes()
features.summary: Tests whether an array contains a value.

migration.note: includes can find NaN; indexOf cannot.

features.title: Exponentiation operator
features.summary: The ** operator and the **= assignment operator.

migration.note: ** is right-associative: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 2 ** 9.

features.title: async functions and await
features.summary: async functions return promises, and await pauses them until a promise settles.

migration.note: An async function always returns a promise, even when it returns a plain value.

features.title: Object.values() and Object.entries()
features.summary: Return an object's own enumerable property values, or its key-value pairs.

features.title: Object rest and spread
features.summary: Rest and spread syntax for object properties: { ...a, ...b } and const { x, ...rest } = obj.

migration.note: Spread defines properties on the new object; Object.assign calls setters on its target.

features.title: Array.prototype.flat() and flatMap()
features.summary: Flatten nested arrays, or map and flatten in one step.

migration.note: flat() flattens one level by default; pass Infinity to flatten completely.

features.title: Optional catch binding
features.summary: A catch clause can omit the error variable when it is not needed.

features.title: Optional chaining
features.summary: The ?. operator stops and returns undefined when the left side is null or undefined.

migration.note: && stops on any falsy value (0, empty string, false). ?. stops only on null and undefined.

features.title: Nullish coalescing
features.summary: The ?? operator returns its right side only when the left side is null or undefined.

migration.note: || also replaces 0, empty strings and false. ?? replaces only null and undefined.

features.title: BigInt
features.summary: Integers of arbitrary size, written with an n suffix such as 123n.

features.title: Dynamic import()
features.summary: import() loads a module at run time and returns a promise for its namespace.

node.note: Earlier releases that supported it: 12.17.0 to 12.19.0.

features.title: Logical assignment operators
features.summary: The &&=, ||= and ??= operators assign only when a condition on the left side holds.

migration.note: ||= replaces any falsy value. Use ??= to replace only null or undefined.

features.title: String.prototype.replaceAll()
features.summary: Replaces every occurrence of a string or pattern.

migration.note: A string argument is matched literally. A regular expression argument must have the g flag.

features.title: Class fields and private members
features.summary: Field declarations in class bodies, including #private fields and methods, static fields and static blocks.

migration.note: A #private field is enforced by the language. An _underscore name is only a convention.

features.title: Top-level await
features.summary: await can be used at the top level of a module.

migration.note: Only valid in module code.

features.title: Array.prototype.at()
features.summary: Reads an element by index, counting from the end when the index is negative. Also on strings and typed arrays.

features.title: Object.hasOwn()
features.summary: Tests whether an object has an own property, without going through the prototype.

features.title: findLast() and findLastIndex()
features.summary: Search an array from the end.

features.title: toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced() and with()
features.summary: Copying versions of sort, reverse and splice, plus with() to replace one element.

migration.note: sort(), reverse() and splice() change the array in place. The new methods return a copy.

features.title: Object.groupBy() and Map.groupBy()
features.summary: Group the items of an iterable by a key function.

migration.note: Object.groupBy returns an object with a null prototype.

features.title: Promise.withResolvers()
features.summary: Returns a promise together with its resolve and reject functions.

features.title: Iterator helpers
features.summary: Iterator methods such as map, filter, take, drop, flatMap and toArray, which work lazily.

migration.note: Helpers pull values one at a time. Spreading into an array first evaluates the whole sequence.

features.title: Set methods
features.summary: union(), intersection(), difference(), symmetricDifference(), isSubsetOf(), isSupersetOf() and isDisjointFrom().

features.title: Promise.try()
features.summary: Calls a function and always returns a promise, even if the function throws synchronously.

migration.note: A synchronous exception becomes a rejection.

features.title: Import attributes and JSON modules
features.summary: A with { type: "json" } clause on imports, used to import JSON modules.

features.title: Array.fromAsync()
features.summary: Builds an array from an async iterable and returns a promise for it.

features.title: Error.isError()
features.summary: Reliably tests whether a value is an error object.

node.note: Partly supported from 24.0.0, where it returned false for DOMException instances (Node.js issue 56497). Fully supported from 24.3.0.

migration.note: instanceof fails for errors created in another realm, such as an iframe.

features.title: using declarations
features.summary: using and await using declarations dispose of a resource automatically when the block ends.

migration.note: The resource needs a [Symbol.dispose]() method.

features.title: Temporal
features.summary: A modern date and time API that fixes many problems of the Date object.

features.title: Iterators and generators
features.summary: The iterator protocol, for...of loops, and generator functions (function*) that produce values with yield.

migration.note: A generator function returns an iterator that works with for...of and spread.

features.title: Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet
features.summary: Keyed and unique-value collections whose keys can be any value, not just strings.

migration.modern:
const counts = new Map();
words.forEach((word) => counts.set(word, (counts.get(word) || 0) + 1));
migration.note: A plain object only has string and symbol keys, and inherits properties such as toString.

features.title: Symbols
features.summary: A primitive type for unique property keys, including well-known symbols such as Symbol.iterator.

features.title: Proxy and Reflect
features.summary: Proxy objects intercept operations on another object, and Reflect exposes those operations as functions.

features.title: Typed arrays
features.summary: Fixed-type views over binary data, such as Uint8Array and Float64Array.

features.title: Array.from(), Array.of(), find() and friends
features.summary: Array.from, Array.of, find, findIndex, fill, copyWithin and the keys, values and entries iterators.

migration.note: Array.from also accepts any iterable and an optional mapping function.

features.title: Shorthand and computed object properties
features.summary: { name, age } shorthand, method shorthand, and [expression] computed property names in object literals.

migration.legacy:
var user = { name: name, age: age };
user[prefix + "Id"] = id;

features.title: Number and Math additions
features.summary: Number.isInteger, Number.isSafeInteger, Number.EPSILON, Math.trunc, Math.sign, Math.hypot and related functions.

migration.legacy: var isInt = typeof x === "number" && isFinite(x) && Math.floor(x) === x;
migration.note: Number.isNaN and Number.isFinite do not convert their argument, unlike the global isNaN and isFinite.

features.title: Unicode code point support
features.summary: String.fromCodePoint(), codePointAt(), normalize(), \u{...} escapes and the u flag for regular expressions.

features.title: padStart() and padEnd()
features.summary: Pad a string to a minimum length at the start or the end.

features.title: Trailing commas in parameters
features.summary: A trailing comma is allowed in function parameter lists and call arguments.

migration.note: Adding a parameter later changes only one line in a diff.

features.title: SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics
features.summary: Memory shared between agents and atomic operations for coordinating access to it.

features.title: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors()
features.summary: Returns the full property descriptors of an object, including getters and setters.

features.title: Async iteration and async generators
features.summary: for await...of loops and async function* generators for sequences that arrive over time.

migration.note: The source must be an async iterable, meaning it has a Symbol.asyncIterator method.

features.title: Promise.prototype.finally()
features.summary: Runs a callback when a promise settles, whether it was fulfilled or rejected.

migration.note: The callback receives no arguments, and the original result or error passes through.

features.title: Named capture groups
features.summary: (?<name>...) captures that can be read from the groups property of a match.

features.title: Lookbehind assertions
features.summary: (?<=...) and (?<!...) match text only when it is preceded, or not preceded, by a pattern.

migration.legacy:
var match = /\$(\d+)/.exec(text);
var amount = match && match[1];
migration.modern:
var match = /(?<=\$)\d+/.exec(text);
var amount = match && match[0];
migration.note: The lookbehind is checked but not included in the match.

features.title: Unicode property escapes
features.summary: \p{...} and \P{...} match characters by Unicode property, with the u flag.

migration.note: The older pattern only covers ASCII letters.

features.title: The s (dotAll) flag
features.summary: With the s flag, . also matches line terminators.

features.title: Object.fromEntries()
features.summary: Builds an object from key-value pairs. It is the inverse of Object.entries().

features.title: trimStart() and trimEnd()
features.summary: Standard names for trimming one side of a string. They replace the older trimLeft() and trimRight().

migration.note: trimLeft and trimRight are still available as aliases in Annex B.

features.title: Array.prototype.sort()
features.summary: Sorts an array in place. The default order compares elements as strings.

ecmascript.note: sort must be stable: elements that compare as equal keep their original relative order.
The algorithm is specified more precisely, so fewer cases leave the result order up to the implementation.

features.title: Function.prototype.toString()
features.summary: Returns a string describing a function.

ecmascript.note: It must return the function's original source text, or a standard placeholder for built-in and bound functions.

features.title: Symbol.prototype.description
features.summary: Reads the description a symbol was created with.

features.title: String.prototype.matchAll()
features.summary: Returns an iterator over every match of a global regular expression, including capture groups.

migration.note: The regular expression must have the g flag.

features.title: Promise.allSettled()
features.summary: Waits for every promise to settle and reports each outcome, without stopping at the first rejection.

features.title: globalThis
features.summary: A standard way to reach the global object in any environment.

migration.legacy: var root = typeof window !== "undefined" ? window : typeof global !== "undefined" ? global : this;

features.title: import.meta
features.summary: An object, filled in by the host, that carries information about the current module.

node.note: The engine accepts the syntax from 10.4.0, but import.meta only works inside ES modules, which Node.js runs without a flag from 13.2.0.

features.title: export * as namespace
features.summary: Re-exports a whole module as a single named export.

migration.legacy:
import * as utils from "./utils.js";
export { utils };

features.title: Promise.any() and AggregateError
features.summary: Resolves with the first fulfilled promise, or rejects with an AggregateError holding every reason.

features.title: WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry
features.summary: References that do not keep an object alive, and callbacks that run after an object is collected.

features.title: Numeric separators
features.summary: Underscores in numeric literals, such as 1_000_000, to make long numbers readable.

features.title: Private brand checks (#x in obj)
features.summary: Tests whether an object has a given private field, without risking an error.

features.title: RegExp match indices (d flag)
features.summary: With the d flag, a match also reports the start and end index of each capture.

features.title: Error cause
features.summary: new Error(message, { cause }) records the error that led to this one.

migration.legacy:
var wrapped = new Error("Load failed: " + err.message);
wrapped.cause = err;
migration.modern: const wrapped = new Error("Load failed", { cause: err });

features.title: Hashbang comments
features.summary: A #! line at the very start of a file is treated as a comment, so scripts can be executable.

features.title: Symbols as weak collection keys
features.summary: Most symbols can be used as WeakMap keys and WeakSet or WeakRef targets.

features.title: Resizable and transferable ArrayBuffers
features.summary: ArrayBuffers that can be resized in place, or transferred to a new owner with transfer().

features.title: RegExp v flag
features.summary: The v flag adds set operations and string literals inside character classes.

features.title: isWellFormed() and toWellFormed()
features.summary: Check whether a string contains lone surrogates, or replace them with U+FFFD.

features.title: Atomics.waitAsync()
features.summary: Waits for a change to shared memory without blocking the thread.

features.title: RegExp.escape()
features.summary: Escapes a string so it can be used safely inside a regular expression.

features.title: Regular expression modifiers
features.summary: Turn flags such as i on or off for part of a pattern, for example (?i:abc).

features.title: Float16Array and Math.f16round()
features.summary: A 16-bit floating-point typed array, with DataView getFloat16 and setFloat16.

features.title: Math.sumPrecise()
features.summary: Adds numbers and returns the correctly rounded total, avoiding the error that builds up in a running sum.

migration.legacy: const total = numbers.reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0);
migration.note: A running sum rounds at every step. sumPrecise rounds once, at the end.

features.title: Uint8Array base64 and hex
features.summary: toBase64(), toHex(), and the matching fromBase64() and fromHex() for converting bytes to and from text.

features.title: JSON source text access
features.summary: JSON.parse revivers can see the original source text of a value, and JSON.rawJSON() writes numbers exactly.

features.title: Iterator.concat()
features.summary: Joins several iterables into one iterator.

features.title: Map getOrInsert() and getOrInsertComputed()
features.summary: Reads a key, adding a default or a computed value first if it is missing. Also on WeakMap.

features.title: Atomics.pause()
features.summary: A hint that the current agent is busy-waiting, so the processor can save power.

features.title: Joint iteration
features.summary: Iterate several iterators together in lockstep.

features.title: CommonJS modules (require and module.exports)
features.summary: The module system Node.js started with: require() loads a module and module.exports defines what it shares.

migration.legacy:
const fs = require("fs");
module.exports = { read: (file) => fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8") };
migration.modern:
import fs from "fs";
export const read = (file) => fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
migration.note: ES modules need a .mjs file name, or "type": "module" in the nearest package.json.

features.title: Import assertions (assert { type })
features.summary: The earlier syntax for importing JSON modules, import data from "./data.json" assert { type: "json" }.

node.note: Import assertions stopped working. Use the with keyword from import attributes instead.

migration.note: Import attributes need Node.js 18.20 or 20.10 and later.

features.title: Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe() and Buffer.from()
features.summary: Safe ways to create a Buffer: a zero-filled one of a given size, an uninitialised one, or a copy of existing data.

features.title: new Buffer() and Buffer()
features.summary: The original Buffer constructor, which could be called with a size, a string, an array or another buffer.

node.note: Printing a runtime warning from 10.0.0 for code outside node_modules (DEP0005), because the constructor raises security and usability concerns.

migration.legacy:
const zeroed = new Buffer(16);
const copy = new Buffer("text", "utf8");
migration.modern:
const zeroed = Buffer.alloc(16);
const copy = Buffer.from("text", "utf8");
migration.note: Buffer.alloc() fills the buffer with zeros. Buffer.allocUnsafe() does not, and is faster.

features.title: crypto.createCipheriv() and createDecipheriv()
features.summary: Create a cipher or decipher from an explicit key and initialization vector.

features.title: crypto.createCipher() and createDecipher()
features.summary: Create a cipher or decipher from a password, deriving the key internally.

node.note: Removed because they used a weak key derivation function (unsalted MD5) and a static initialization vector.

migration.note: Store the salt and the IV with the encrypted data. Data encrypted with createCipher() cannot be decrypted by this code.

features.title: fs.exists()
features.summary: Reports through a callback whether a path exists.

node.note: Deprecated since v1.0.0, in the io.js line that merged into Node.js 4. Use fs.access() or fs.stat(), or simply try the operation and handle the error.

migration.note: Checking and then using a file can race with other processes. Opening the file and handling the error avoids that.

features.title: util.isArray()
features.summary: An early helper for testing whether a value is an array.

node.note: Deprecated since v4.0.0. Use Array.isArray(). The function is still present.

features.title: util.promisify()
features.summary: Turns a function that takes an error-first callback into one that returns a promise.

features.title: fs.promises
features.summary: Promise-returning versions of the file system functions, also available as fs/promises.

features.title: fetch()
features.summary: The Fetch API for HTTP requests, available as a global function.

features.title: AbortController
features.summary: Signals that an operation, such as a fetch, should be cancelled.

features.title: structuredClone()
features.summary: Makes a deep copy of a value, including Map, Set, Date and nested objects.

features.title: node:test
features.summary: A test runner built into Node.js.

features.title: print statement
features.summary: The Python 2 statement form of print, as in print "total", n.

python.note: print is a function in Python 3, so the statement form is a SyntaxError.

migration.note: Redirecting with print >>sys.stderr became the file= keyword argument.

features.title: unicode type and u"" literals
features.summary: Python 2 had separate str (bytes) and unicode types, with u"" for Unicode text literals.

python.note: str now holds Unicode text and bytes holds binary data, so there is no separate unicode type. The u"" prefix was accepted again in Python 3.3 (PEP 414).

migration.note: Decode bytes to get text, and encode text to get bytes.

features.title: Division with /
features.summary: In Python 2, / on two integers truncated the result, so 7 / 2 was 3.

python.note: / always returns a float, so 7 / 2 is 3.5. Use // for floor division.

migration.legacy: average = total / count  # integer division when both are ints
migration.modern: average = total // count  # floor division, as before
migration.note: Use // wherever the old truncating result is wanted.

features.title: dict.has_key()
features.summary: Tests whether a dictionary contains a key.

python.note: dict.has_key() was removed. Use the in operator.

features.title: xrange()
features.summary: A lazy sequence of integers. In Python 2, range() built a full list.

python.note: range() now returns a lazy sequence like the old xrange(), and xrange() was removed.

features.title: raw_input()
features.summary: Reads a line of text from the user. In Python 2, input() evaluated what was typed.

python.note: raw_input() was renamed to input(), and the old input() that evaluated the text was removed.

features.title: except X, e
features.summary: The Python 2 way to name a caught exception: except ValueError, err.

python.note: Only except X as e is accepted. (Python 3.14 allows except A, B without parentheses, but with a different meaning: it catches both types.)

migration.note: The as form has worked since Python 2.6.

features.title: exec statement
features.summary: The Python 2 statement form of exec, as in exec code in namespace.

python.note: exec is a function in Python 3, so the statement form is a SyntaxError.

features.title: Backtick repr
features.summary: Backticks around an expression, as in `value`, produced its repr().

python.note: Backticks were removed. Call repr() instead.

features.title: <> operator
features.summary: An alternative spelling of !=.

python.note: <> was removed. Use !=.

features.title: long type and the L suffix
features.summary: Python 2 had a separate long type for large integers, written with an L suffix such as 10000000000L.

python.note: int is now arbitrary precision, so the long type and the L suffix were removed.

features.title: Old-style classes
features.summary: In Python 2, a class that did not inherit from object was an old-style class with different rules.

python.note: Every class is new-style and inherits from object, so (object) is no longer needed.

migration.legacy:
class Point(object):  # needed in Python 2 to get a new-style class
    pass

features.title: dict.iteritems(), iterkeys() and itervalues()
features.summary: Dictionary methods that returned iterators in Python 2.

python.note: keys(), values() and items() now return lightweight views, and the iter* methods were removed.

migration.legacy:
for key, value in table.iteritems():
    use(key, value)
migration.modern:
for key, value in table.items():
    use(key, value)

features.title: cmp(), __cmp__ and cmp= sorting
features.summary: A three-way comparison function, the __cmp__ method, and the cmp argument to sort().

python.note: cmp() and __cmp__ were removed. Ordering uses rich comparisons and sort() takes key=. functools.cmp_to_key() wraps an old comparison function.

features.title: Implicit relative imports
features.summary: Inside a package, import sibling found a module next to the current one without a dot.

python.note: Imports are absolute by default, so a sibling module needs from . import sibling or its full package path.

migration.legacy: import helpers  # found a module next to this file

features.title: Standard library reorganisation
features.summary: Many modules were renamed, merged or moved into packages (PEP 3108), such as ConfigParser, Queue and urllib2.

python.note: Modules were renamed to lowercase names or grouped into packages, for example ConfigParser to configparser, Queue to queue, and urllib2 into the urllib package.

features.title: print() function
features.summary: print is an ordinary function with sep, end, file and flush keyword arguments.

python.note: Python 2.6 and 2.7 can use it with from __future__ import print_function.

migration.note: sep, end, file and flush are keyword arguments.

features.title: Text and bytes
features.summary: str holds Unicode text. bytes and bytearray hold binary data, and mixing the two raises TypeError.

migration.legacy: data = "abc"  # was a byte string in Python 2
migration.modern: data = b"abc"  # a bytes literal for binary data
migration.note: Convert explicitly: text.encode("utf-8") gives bytes, and data.decode("utf-8") gives text.

features.title: nonlocal
features.summary: Lets an inner function rebind a variable in the nearest enclosing function.

migration.modern:
def counter():
    count = 0
    def increment():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return increment

features.title: Keyword-only arguments
features.summary: Parameters after a bare * or *args can only be passed by name.

migration.modern:
def connect(host, *, timeout=10):
    return open_socket(host, timeout)

features.title: Function annotations
features.summary: Expressions after parameters and after -> are stored in __annotations__. The language gives them no meaning of their own.

features.title: Extended iterable unpacking
features.summary: A starred name in an assignment collects the remaining items, as in first, *rest = items.

features.title: collections.OrderedDict
features.summary: A dictionary that remembers insertion order. It also has move_to_end() and order-sensitive equality.

features.title: concurrent.futures
features.summary: ThreadPoolExecutor and ProcessPoolExecutor, which run calls in a pool and return Future objects.

migration.modern:

features.title: Tail expression temporary scope
features.summary: When the temporary values created in the last expression of a block are dropped.

edition.note: Temporaries in the tail expression of a function, closure or block may be dropped before the local variables, and are sometimes not extended to the next larger temporary scope.

features.title: Newly unsafe functions
features.summary: Standard library functions that were safe to call but can cause undefined behaviour, such as std::env::set_var.

edition.note: std::env::set_var, std::env::remove_var and std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::before_exec are unsafe to call.

features.title: Match ergonomics reservations
features.summary: Rules about writing mut, ref and & inside patterns that rely on default binding modes.

edition.note: Writing mut, ref or ref mut on a binding, or a reference pattern, is an error when the surrounding pattern relies on match ergonomics.

features.title: Macro fragment specifiers
features.summary: What the expr fragment specifier matches in macro_rules macros.

edition.note: expr also matches const blocks and _ expressions. expr_2021 keeps the old behaviour.

features.title: Classes
features.summary: Reference types that bundle data and behaviour, with single inheritance, fields, methods, properties and events.

features.title: Structs
features.summary: Value types that are copied on assignment, suited to small data holders; they can have fields, methods and constructors but no inheritance.

features.title: Interfaces
features.summary: Contracts that list members a type promises to provide; a class or struct can implement any number of them.

features.title: Events
features.summary: Members that let a type announce that something happened, with subscribers attached through += and -=.

features.title: Properties
features.summary: Members that read and write like fields but run code in get and set accessors.

features.title: Delegates
features.summary: Type-safe references to methods, the basis of callbacks and events.

features.title: Attributes
features.summary: Declarative metadata attached to types and members in square brackets, readable by tools and through reflection.

features.title: foreach disposes its enumerator
features.summary: A foreach loop calls Dispose on its enumerator when the loop ends, even if it exits early or throws.

features.title: Generics
features.summary: Types and methods parameterised by type, written List<T>, giving compile-time type safety without casts or boxing.

features.title: Partial types
features.summary: A class, struct or interface split across several source files with the partial keyword and merged by the compiler.

features.title: Nullable value types
features.summary: T? wraps a value type so it can also hold null, as in int? or DateTime?.

features.title: Anonymous methods
features.summary: Inline method bodies written with the delegate keyword and no name, which can capture local variables.

features.title: Iterators (yield)
features.summary: A method using yield return (or yield break) that produces a sequence lazily, one element at a time.

features.title: Static classes
features.summary: A class marked static that cannot be instantiated or inherited and holds only static members.

features.title: Separate accessibility for get and set
features.summary: One accessor of a property can be more restricted than the other, as in public get with private set.

features.title: Lambda expressions
features.summary: Compact anonymous functions written x => expression or (x, y) => { statements }, convertible to delegates or expression trees.

features.title: Implicitly typed locals (var)
features.summary: var lets the compiler infer a local variable's type from its initialiser; the variable stays statically typed.

features.title: Extension methods
features.summary: Static methods in a static class that are called as if they were instance methods of another type, using this on the first parameter.

features.title: Object and collection initializers
features.summary: Set properties or add collection items right after new, as in new Point { X = 1, Y = 2 }.

features.title: Auto-implemented properties
features.summary: A property written { get; set; } for which the compiler generates the backing field.

features.title: Anonymous types
features.summary: Unnamed reference types created with new { Name = value }, used mainly for query results.

features.title: Query expressions (LINQ)
features.summary: SQL-like from, where, select and orderby syntax that the compiler translates into LINQ method calls.

features.title: Expression trees
features.summary: Code represented as a data structure that providers such as LINQ to SQL can inspect and translate.

features.title: Partial methods
features.summary: A method declared in one part of a partial type and optionally implemented in another; with no implementation the calls are removed.

features.title: dynamic
features.summary: A type whose members are looked up at run time instead of compile time, used for COM interop and loosely typed data.

features.title: Named and optional arguments
features.summary: Arguments can be passed by name, and parameters can have default values so callers may omit them.

features.title: Generic covariance and contravariance
features.summary: Interfaces and delegates can be marked out (covariant) or in (contravariant) so IEnumerable<Derived> converts to IEnumerable<Base>.

features.title: foreach loop variable
features.summary: The foreach iteration variable is read-only, and since C# 5 each iteration gets its own copy, so lambdas created in the loop capture that iteration's value.

csharp.note: In C# 4 and earlier all iterations shared one variable, so a closure created in the loop saw the last value; since C# 5 each iteration has its own variable. A for loop still shares its variable.

features.title: async and await
features.summary: async methods return Task and use await to wait for work without blocking the calling thread.

features.title: Caller info attributes
features.summary: CallerMemberName, CallerFilePath and CallerLineNumber attributes make the compiler pass the caller's name, file and line as argument values.

features.title: using static
features.summary: using static imports a type's static members so they can be called without the type name.

features.title: Exception filters (when)
features.summary: A catch clause can add when (condition) and only catches the exception if the condition is true, before the stack unwinds.

features.title: Auto-property initializers
features.summary: An auto-property can have an initial value, as in public int Count { get; } = 1;, and a getter-only one can be set in the constructor.

features.title: Expression-bodied members
features.summary: A method or property whose body is a single expression can be written with => instead of braces.

csharp.note: Expression bodies were extended to constructors, finalizers, and property and indexer accessors.

features.title: Null-conditional operators (?.)
features.summary: ?. and ?[] stop evaluating and produce null when the left side is null, instead of throwing NullReferenceException.

features.title: String interpolation
features.summary: $"...{expression}..." builds a string by embedding expressions directly in the text.

features.title: nameof
features.summary: nameof(x) produces the name of a variable, type or member as a string that stays correct when you rename it.

features.title: Index initializers
features.summary: Collection initializers can set elements by index or key, as in new Dictionary<string,int> { ["a"] = 1 }.

features.title: await in catch and finally
features.summary: await is allowed inside catch and finally blocks.

features.title: out variable declarations
features.summary: An out argument can be declared at the call, as in int.TryParse(s, out var n), and the variable is usable after the call.

features.title: Tuples
features.summary: Lightweight value-type groupings written (int, string) with optional element names, backed by System.ValueTuple.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It compiles against .NET Framework from 4.7 but not before (CS8179); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

netfx.note: System.ValueTuple is part of the framework from 4.7; tuple syntax does not compile against the 4.6.2 and earlier reference assemblies.

features.title: Deconstruction
features.summary: Split a tuple, or any type with a Deconstruct method, into separate variables with var (a, b) = pair;.

features.title: Pattern matching (is and switch patterns)
features.summary: The is operator and switch can test a value's type and shape and bind variables, as in o is int n.

csharp.note: Patterns can now be matched against a value whose type is a generic type parameter.

features.title: Local functions
features.summary: A method declared inside another method that can use the enclosing method's locals.

features.title: Digit separators and binary literals
features.summary: Underscores in numeric literals (1_000_000) and binary literals (0b1010) make long numbers readable.

csharp.note: A separator is allowed straight after the base prefix, as in 0x_FF or 0b_1.

features.title: Ref locals and ref returns
features.summary: Methods can return a reference to storage, and locals can hold such a reference, to avoid copying large structs.

csharp.note: Ref returns can be ref readonly, and a conditional expression can produce a ref (ref flag ? ref a : ref b).
A ref local can be reassigned to refer to a different variable, as in r = ref other;.

features.title: Discards
features.summary: The underscore _ ignores an out argument, tuple element or lambda parameter you do not need.

features.title: throw expressions
features.summary: throw can be used as an expression, for example after ?? or in a conditional or expression-bodied member.

features.title: async Main
features.summary: Main can be async and return Task or Task<int>, so a program can await at its entry point.

features.title: default literal
features.summary: default without a type, as in int x = default;, takes its type from the context.

features.title: Inferred tuple element names
features.summary: A tuple built as (a, b) takes its element names from the variables a and b.

features.title: in parameters
features.summary: An in parameter passes a value by read-only reference, avoiding a copy of a large struct.

features.title: readonly struct
features.summary: A struct marked readonly guarantees it cannot change after construction, letting the compiler avoid defensive copies.

features.title: ref struct
features.summary: A struct that can only live on the stack, which makes it safe to hold references to stack memory such as Span<T>.

features.title: Non-trailing named arguments
features.summary: Named arguments may be followed by positional ones as long as the names are in the right position.

features.title: private protected
features.summary: An accessibility level meaning the member is visible only in the containing class and derived classes in the same assembly.

features.title: unmanaged, Enum and Delegate constraints
features.summary: Generic constraints where T : unmanaged, System.Enum or System.Delegate restrict a type argument to those kinds of types.

features.title: stackalloc initializers
features.summary: A stackalloc array can be initialised inline, as in stackalloc int[] { 1, 2, 3 }.

features.title: Fixed buffers without pinning
features.summary: Elements of a fixed-size buffer field in a movable struct can be accessed without a fixed statement.

features.title: fixed on any type with GetPinnableReference
features.summary: A fixed statement works on any type that has an accessible GetPinnableReference method.

features.title: Tuple equality (== and !=)
features.summary: Tuples can be compared with == and !=, element by element.

features.title: Expression variables in initializers and queries
features.summary: out variables and pattern variables can be declared in field initializers, constructor initializers and query clauses.

features.title: Attributes on auto-property backing fields
features.summary: An attribute with the field: target on an auto-property is applied to its compiler-generated backing field.

features.title: readonly members
features.summary: Individual struct members can be marked readonly to promise they do not modify the struct's state.

features.title: Default interface members
features.summary: An interface can provide a default implementation of a member that implementing types inherit unless they override it.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS8701); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Switch expressions
features.summary: A switch written as an expression, value switch { pattern => result, _ => fallback }, that produces a value.

features.title: Property patterns
features.summary: A pattern that tests properties of an object, as in person is { Age: >= 18 }.

features.title: Positional and tuple patterns
features.summary: A pattern that matches the parts of a tuple or deconstructable type by position, as in point is (0, 0).

features.title: using declarations
features.summary: using var x = ...; disposes the variable at the end of the enclosing scope, without an extra block.

features.title: Static local functions
features.summary: A local function marked static cannot capture the enclosing method's variables.

features.title: Disposable ref structs
features.summary: A ref struct with a public Dispose method can be used in a using statement without implementing IDisposable.

features.title: Nullable reference types
features.summary: Reference types are non-nullable by default and string? marks the ones that may be null, with compiler warnings for likely null errors.

features.title: Async streams (await foreach)
features.summary: await foreach consumes an IAsyncEnumerable<T>, and an async method can yield return elements as they become available.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0234); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

dotnet.note: IAsyncEnumerable<T> and IAsyncEnumerator<T>, which the C# 8 syntax needs, arrive with .NET Core 3.0.

features.title: Indices and ranges
features.summary: The ^ operator counts from the end and .. selects a range, as in items[^1] and items[1..3].

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0518); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

dotnet.note: System.Index and System.Range, which the C# 8 syntax compiles to, arrive with .NET Core 3.0.

features.title: Null-coalescing assignment (??=)
features.summary: a ??= b assigns b to a only when a is null.

features.title: Unmanaged constructed types
features.summary: A generic struct whose type arguments are unmanaged types is itself unmanaged, so pointers to it are allowed.

features.title: @$ interpolated verbatim strings
features.summary: @$"..." and $@"..." can be written in either order to combine verbatim and interpolated strings.

features.title: Records
features.summary: A type declared with record whose equality, printing and with-copies are based on its values rather than its identity.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0518); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS0518); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it. Defining System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsExternalInit in your own code makes it compile there; this was checked at compile time only.

features.title: Init-only setters
features.summary: An init accessor can be set only while the object is being created, giving immutable properties with initialiser syntax.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0518); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS0518); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it. Defining System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsExternalInit in your own code makes it compile there; this was checked at compile time only.

features.title: Top-level statements
features.summary: A program's entry-point statements can be written directly in a file, without a Main method or class.

features.title: Relational and logical patterns
features.summary: Patterns can compare with <, >, <=, >= and combine with and, or and not, as in x is > 0 and < 10.

features.title: nint and nuint
features.summary: nint and nuint are integers sized to the platform's pointer width.

features.title: Function pointers
features.summary: delegate*<int, void> declares an unmanaged-style pointer to a method that can be called without delegate overhead.

features.title: Module initializers
features.summary: A static method marked [ModuleInitializer] runs once, before any other code in the assembly.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0234); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS0234); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it. Defining System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializerAttribute in your own code makes it compile there; this was checked at compile time only.

features.title: Partial methods with any signature
features.summary: Partial methods can have any return type, out parameters and accessibility, as long as an implementation is supplied.

features.title: Target-typed new
features.summary: new() without a type creates an object of the type the context expects.

features.title: Static anonymous functions
features.summary: A lambda or anonymous method marked static cannot capture local variables or this.

features.title: Target-typed conditional expressions
features.summary: The ?: operator can take its type from the context when its two branches have no common type.

features.title: Covariant return types
features.summary: An overriding method can return a more derived type than the method it overrides.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS8830); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS8830); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Extension GetEnumerator in foreach
features.summary: foreach works on a type that gets its GetEnumerator method from an extension method.

features.title: Lambda discard parameters
features.summary: Several unused lambda parameters can all be written _.

features.title: Attributes on local functions
features.summary: Attributes can be applied to local functions, their parameters and their type parameters.

features.title: Record structs
features.summary: record struct gives a value type the generated equality, ToString and with-expression support of records.

features.title: global using
features.summary: A using directive marked global applies to every file in the project.

features.title: File-scoped namespaces
features.summary: namespace N; applies to the whole file and removes one level of indentation.

features.title: Extended property patterns
features.summary: A property pattern can reach nested properties with a dot, as in o is { Address.City: "Oslo" }.

features.title: Lambda natural type, return type and attributes
features.summary: Lambdas can have attributes and an explicit return type, and a lambda with explicit parameter types has a natural delegate type that var can use.

features.title: Constant interpolated strings
features.summary: A const string can be built with interpolation when every embedded value is itself a constant string.

features.title: sealed ToString in records
features.summary: A record can seal its ToString override so derived records do not regenerate it.

features.title: Mixed assignment and declaration in deconstruction
features.summary: A deconstruction can assign to existing variables and declare new ones in the same statement.

features.title: Parameterless struct constructors
features.summary: A struct can declare its own parameterless constructor and field initialisers.

features.title: Interpolated string handlers
features.summary: Types marked [InterpolatedStringHandler] let an interpolated string be built without allocating, for example in logging.

features.title: CallerArgumentExpression
features.summary: [CallerArgumentExpression] fills a parameter with the source text of the argument passed for another parameter.

features.title: Raw string literals
features.summary: Strings delimited by three or more double quotes can contain quotes and newlines without escaping.

features.title: Static abstract interface members and generic math
features.summary: An interface can declare static abstract members that implementing types must provide, which is what makes generic math possible.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS8919); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS8919); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Generic attributes
features.summary: An attribute class can be generic, so [Validate<int>] carries its type argument.

features.title: UTF-8 string literals
features.summary: A string literal followed by u8 is a UTF-8 encoded ReadOnlySpan<byte>.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0234); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Newlines in interpolation holes
features.summary: The expression inside an interpolation hole in $"{...}" can span several lines.

features.title: List patterns
features.summary: Patterns match arrays and lists by their elements, as in values is [1, 2, ..].

features.title: file-local types
features.summary: A type marked file is visible only within its own source file.

features.title: required members
features.summary: A member marked required must be set by the object initialiser or constructor that creates the object.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0656); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS0656); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it. Defining RequiredMemberAttribute, CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute and SetsRequiredMembersAttribute in your own code makes it compile there; this was checked at compile time only.

features.title: Auto-default structs
features.summary: A struct constructor no longer has to assign every field; the compiler sets the rest to their defaults.

features.title: Pattern match Span<char> on a constant string
features.summary: A Span<char> or ReadOnlySpan<char> can be matched against a constant string in a pattern.

features.title: nameof of parameters in attributes
features.summary: nameof can refer to a method's parameters and type parameters inside attributes on that method.

features.title: ref fields and scoped
features.summary: A ref struct can declare a ref field, and the scoped modifier limits how long a reference may live.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS9064); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS9064); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Unsigned right shift (>>>)
features.summary: The >>> operator shifts right without sign extension.

features.title: User-defined checked operators
features.summary: A type can define separate checked and unchecked versions of an arithmetic operator.

features.title: Primary constructors
features.summary: Parameters written after a class or struct name are in scope throughout the type, like a constructor whose parameters are captured.

features.title: Collection expressions
features.summary: [1, 2, 3] creates an array, list, span or other collection type, and .. spreads another collection into it.

features.title: Inline arrays
features.summary: A struct marked [InlineArray(n)] holds n elements of one type in a fixed-size buffer that can be indexed like an array.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0234); netstandard 2.1 rejects it (CS0234); .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Default values for lambda parameters
features.summary: A lambda parameter can have a default value, and a lambda can use params.

features.title: ref readonly parameters
features.summary: A ref readonly parameter is passed by reference and cannot be modified; unlike in, callers are expected to write ref or in at the call.

features.title: using alias for any type
features.summary: A using alias can name any type, including tuples and pointer types, as in using Point = (int X, int Y);.

features.title: nameof with instance members
features.summary: nameof can name an instance member of a field or property, as in nameof(f.ToString), in places such as field initializers and attributes where this is not available.

features.title: ExperimentalAttribute
features.summary: [Experimental] marks a type or member as experimental, so using it produces a diagnostic that must be suppressed on purpose.

features.title: params collections
features.summary: A params parameter can be any collection type such as Span<T>, ReadOnlySpan<T> or IEnumerable<T>, not just an array.

features.title: System.Threading.Lock and lock
features.summary: The lock statement recognises System.Threading.Lock and uses its dedicated, faster locking instead of Monitor.

features.title: \e escape sequence
features.summary: The \e escape sequence writes the ESC character (U+001B) in a string or char literal.

features.title: Implicit index (^) in object initializers
features.summary: An object initializer can use the from-the-end index ^ for array elements, as in { [^1] = 5 }.

features.title: ref locals and unsafe in iterators and async
features.summary: ref locals and ref struct locals can be used in async methods and iterators as long as they do not live across an await or yield.

features.title: ref struct interfaces and allows ref struct
features.summary: A ref struct can implement interfaces, and a generic parameter marked allows ref struct can be a ref struct.

features.title: Partial properties and indexers
features.summary: Properties and indexers can be declared in one part of a partial type and implemented in another.

features.title: OverloadResolutionPriority
features.summary: [OverloadResolutionPriority] lets a library author prefer one overload over another when more than one applies.

features.title: Extension members
features.summary: An extension block can add extension properties, operators and static members, not only instance methods.

features.title: Null-conditional assignment
features.summary: ?. and ?[] can be on the left of an assignment, so a?.b = c assigns only when a is not null.

features.title: nameof with unbound generic types
features.summary: nameof accepts an unbound generic type such as List<>, and returns the name without type arguments.

features.title: First-class Span conversions
features.summary: Arrays, Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> convert to each other implicitly, including when calling extension methods.

csharp.note: Needs library or runtime support. It does not compile against any .NET Framework 4.5 to 4.8 reference assembly (CS0234); netstandard 2.1 accepts it; .NET 8 and .NET 10 accept it.

features.title: Modifiers on simple lambda parameters
features.summary: A lambda parameter can carry ref, out, in, scoped or ref readonly without writing its type.

features.title: field keyword in properties
features.summary: Inside a property accessor, field refers to the compiler-generated backing field, so you can add logic without declaring one yourself.

features.title: Partial events and constructors
features.summary: Events and instance constructors can be declared in one part of a partial type and implemented in another.

features.title: User-defined compound assignment operators
features.summary: A type can define += and the other compound assignment operators directly, so they update in place instead of calling + and assigning.

features.title: .NET Core cross-platform runtime
features.summary: A cross-platform, open-source .NET runtime and class library for Windows, macOS and Linux, separate from the Windows-only .NET Framework.

features.title: dotnet command-line interface
features.summary: The dotnet command, used to create, restore, build, test, run and publish projects from a terminal.

features.title: .NET Standard 2.0 support
features.summary: .NET Standard 2.0 is supported, so a library built for that API set runs on the runtime.

features.title: Implicit dotnet restore
features.summary: Commands such as dotnet build and dotnet run restore NuGet packages automatically; a separate dotnet restore is no longer needed.

features.title: Span<T> and Memory<T>
features.summary: Span<T> and Memory<T> give safe, allocation-free access to slices of arrays, stack memory and native memory.

features.title: Brotli compression
features.summary: Built-in Brotli compression through BrotliStream, BrotliEncoder and BrotliDecoder.

features.title: dotnet tool (global tools)
features.summary: dotnet tool install -g installs command-line tools distributed as NuGet packages.

features.title: Windows Compatibility Pack
features.summary: A package that provides about 20,000 more Windows-oriented APIs to .NET Core, including System.Drawing, the event log, WMI and Windows services.

features.title: Framework-dependent executables
features.summary: A framework-dependent app can be published as a platform-specific executable that runs against the installed shared runtime.

features.title: Default native executables (apphost)
features.summary: dotnet build and publish produce a native executable for the current platform alongside the app's dll.

features.title: Single-file executables
features.summary: An app and its dependencies can be published as one executable file.

features.title: Assembly trimming
features.summary: The publish step can remove unused assemblies to make a self-contained app smaller.

features.title: Tiered compilation
features.summary: Methods are first compiled quickly and then recompiled with full optimisation when they prove hot, improving start-up and steady-state speed.

features.title: ReadyToRun images
features.summary: Assemblies can be compiled ahead of time to native code in ReadyToRun format to cut JIT work at start-up.

features.title: Major-version runtime roll-forward
features.summary: An app can opt in to run on a newer major runtime version when the exact one it was built for is not installed.

features.title: Local tools
features.summary: Tools can be installed per repository and pinned in a manifest, so each project uses its own versions.

features.title: System.Text.Json
features.summary: A built-in, high-performance JSON reader, writer and serializer in the System.Text.Json namespace.

dotnet.note: Adds support for preserving references and circular references, HttpClient serialization extensions, and reading or writing numbers as quoted strings.

features.title: HTTP/2 in HttpClient
features.summary: HttpClient can send requests over HTTP/2.

features.title: Windows Forms and WPF on .NET Core
features.summary: Windows Forms and WPF apps can run on .NET Core on Windows.

features.title: Platform-dependent hardware intrinsics
features.summary: The System.Runtime.Intrinsics APIs expose CPU-specific instructions such as SSE and AVX for hand-tuned code.

features.title: TLS 1.3 on Linux
features.summary: TLS 1.3 is supported where the operating system's OpenSSL supports it.

features.title: .NET Standard 2.1 support
features.summary: .NET Standard 2.1 is supported, which adds APIs such as Span<T> and the range types for libraries.

features.title: C++/CLI on Windows
features.summary: C++/CLI projects can be built against .NET Core on Windows.

features.title: Source generators
features.summary: Compiler plugins that inspect your code and add generated source files during compilation.

features.title: PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority>
features.summary: PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority> removes elements in order of priority rather than insertion.

features.title: System.Text.Json source generator
features.summary: System.Text.Json can generate serialization code at compile time, which avoids reflection and works with trimming.

features.title: Writeable JSON DOM (JsonNode)
features.summary: JsonNode, JsonObject and JsonArray let you build and edit a JSON document in memory.

features.title: DateOnly and TimeOnly
features.summary: DateOnly and TimeOnly represent a calendar date and a time of day without the other part or a time zone.

features.title: HTTP/3 in HttpClient
features.summary: HttpClient can send requests over HTTP/3 (a preview in this release).

features.title: Hot reload
features.summary: Edit running code and apply the change without restarting the app.

features.title: Crossgen2
features.summary: The ReadyToRun compiler is rewritten as Crossgen2, a managed compiler that replaces the earlier native tool.

features.title: Dynamic profile-guided optimization
features.summary: The runtime can use dynamic profile data gathered while the app runs to optimise hot paths.

features.title: Generic math (INumber<T> and friends)
features.summary: Interfaces such as INumber<T> and IAdditionOperators<T> let one generic algorithm work across every numeric type.

features.title: Regular expression source generator
features.summary: [GeneratedRegex] makes the compiler generate the matching code for a regular expression at build time.

features.title: P/Invoke source generation (LibraryImport)
features.summary: [LibraryImport] generates P/Invoke marshalling code at compile time instead of at run time.

features.title: Publish to a container image
features.summary: dotnet publish can build a container image of an app without a Dockerfile.

features.title: Central package management
features.summary: NuGet package versions for a whole solution can be set in one Directory.Packages.props file.

features.title: Frozen collections
features.summary: FrozenDictionary and FrozenSet are immutable collections optimised for fast lookups after creation.

features.title: SearchValues<T>
features.summary: SearchValues<T> precomputes an optimised way to search spans for any of a set of values.

features.title: TimeProvider
features.summary: TimeProvider is an abstraction over the clock and timers that can be replaced in tests.

features.title: CompositeFormat
features.summary: CompositeFormat parses a format string once so it can be reused for many string.Format calls.

features.title: IMeterFactory (metrics)
features.summary: IMeterFactory creates metrics Meter instances that are scoped to a dependency injection container.

features.title: Keyed dependency injection services
features.summary: Dependency injection services can be registered and resolved by key.

features.title: Source-generated COM interop
features.summary: [GeneratedComInterface] generates COM interop code at compile time.

features.title: Native AOT publishing
features.summary: An app can be compiled ahead of time into a self-contained native executable with no JIT.

features.title: OrderedDictionary<TKey,TValue>
features.summary: OrderedDictionary<TKey,TValue> is a generic dictionary that keeps entries in insertion order and supports access by index.

features.title: ReadOnlySet<T>
features.summary: ReadOnlySet<T> is a read-only wrapper around an ISet<T>.

features.title: Base64Url
features.summary: The Base64Url class encodes and decodes the URL-safe variant of Base64.

features.title: Server-sent events parser
features.summary: System.Net.ServerSentEvents parses text/event-stream responses.

features.title: JsonSchemaExporter
features.summary: JsonSchemaExporter generates a JSON Schema for a .NET type.

features.title: KMAC algorithm
features.summary: Kmac128, Kmac256 and the related classes implement the KMAC message authentication algorithm.

features.title: LINQ CountBy, AggregateBy and Index
features.summary: LINQ gains CountBy and AggregateBy for grouping without building groups, and Index for element-with-position pairs.

features.title: Regex.EnumerateSplits
features.summary: Regex.EnumerateSplits splits a span without allocating an array of strings.

features.title: Persisted dynamic assemblies
features.summary: PersistedAssemblyBuilder lets Reflection.Emit write a dynamically built assembly to disk.

features.title: Managed exception handling by default
features.summary: CoreCLR uses a new exception-handling implementation based on the NativeAOT model, which the documentation measures as 2 to 4 times faster in micro-benchmarks.

features.title: Dynamic adaptation to application sizes (GC)
features.summary: Garbage collection uses a dynamic adaptation to application size by default, instead of the traditional Server GC.

features.title: Post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM)
features.summary: System.Security.Cryptography adds ML-KEM and other post-quantum algorithms.

features.title: WebSocketStream
features.summary: WebSocketStream wraps a WebSocket in the Stream API.

features.title: Strict JSON serialization options
features.summary: JsonSerializerOptions.Strict turns on a strict set of serializer options in one step.

features.title: Async ZIP APIs
features.summary: ZipFile and ZipArchive have async methods for reading and writing archives.

features.title: Numeric ordering for string comparison
features.summary: A comparison option that orders digit sequences in strings by numeric value, so "2" sorts before "10".

features.title: Stack allocation of small arrays
features.summary: The JIT can allocate small arrays of value types on the stack when they do not escape.

features.title: Escape analysis
features.summary: The JIT analyses whether objects escape a method and can allocate non-escaping ones on the stack.

features.title: AVX10.2 support
features.summary: The runtime supports the AVX10.2 instruction set extensions.

features.title: HttpClient
features.summary: HttpClient and the System.Net.Http types give a modern, async-friendly API for sending HTTP requests.

features.title: Asynchronous file operations
features.summary: Stream, StreamReader, StreamWriter and related file classes gain Task-returning async methods such as ReadAsync and WriteAsync.

features.title: ZIP archive API (System.IO.Compression.ZipFile)
features.summary: System.IO.Compression.ZipFile and ZipArchive read and write ZIP archives.

features.title: Regular expression match timeout
features.summary: A Regex can be given a match timeout so a runaway pattern throws RegexMatchTimeoutException instead of hanging.

features.title: TypeInfo reflection split
features.summary: TypeInfo, returned by GetTypeInfo, separates a type's declared members from the full Type object in the reflection API.

features.title: Background garbage collection for servers
features.summary: Background garbage collection is enabled automatically when server garbage collection is used.

features.title: Arrays larger than 2 GB on 64-bit
features.summary: On 64-bit platforms, an opt-in setting allows arrays larger than 2 GB in total size.

features.title: Background JIT compilation
features.summary: Methods can be JIT-compiled on a background thread, which speeds up start-up when multicore JIT is used.

features.title: MEF convention-based programming model
features.summary: The Managed Extensibility Framework can discover parts by naming convention instead of attributes.

features.title: Portable Class Libraries
features.summary: A single library project can target several Microsoft platforms and use the APIs they share.

features.title: On-demand large object heap compaction
features.summary: GCSettings.LargeObjectHeapCompactionMode lets code ask for the large object heap to be compacted on the next full blocking collection.

features.title: Automatic binding redirection
features.summary: Visual Studio can add assembly binding redirects to an app's configuration file automatically.

features.title: DPI-aware resizing in Windows Forms controls
features.summary: Windows Forms controls can resize their internal parts, such as property grid icons, to the system DPI setting when the app opts in through its configuration file.

netfx.note: DPI-aware resizing is extended to more Windows Forms controls.

features.title: Async-aware debugging in Visual Studio
features.summary: The Visual Studio debugger understands async call chains, so Call Stack and Tasks windows show the logical flow.

features.title: HttpResponse.AddOnSendingHeaders
features.summary: HttpResponse.AddOnSendingHeaders lets ASP.NET code run just before response headers are sent.

features.title: Unix time conversion (DateTimeOffset)
features.summary: DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds, ToUnixTimeSeconds and their millisecond variants convert to and from Unix time.

features.title: RSACng and RSA extension methods
