features.summary: RSACng and the RSA certificate extension methods give access to CNG-based RSA keys.

features.title: Task-based response flushing
features.summary: HttpResponse.FlushAsync lets ASP.NET apps flush a response without blocking a thread.

features.title: IReadOnlyCollection<T> on built-in collections
features.summary: More built-in collections, such as Stack<T> and Queue<T>, implement IReadOnlyCollection<T>.

features.title: 64-bit RyuJIT compiler
features.summary: The 64-bit JIT compiler is replaced by RyuJIT, which compiles faster and produces better code.

features.title: SIMD-enabled vector types
features.summary: System.Numerics vector types use the processor's SIMD instructions for faster numeric work, when RyuJIT is in use.

features.title: CultureInfo.CurrentCulture flows across async
features.summary: CultureInfo.CurrentCulture and CurrentUICulture flow with the logical call context across async operations.

features.title: ECDSA X.509 certificates
features.summary: X.509 certificates can provide ECDSA keys, and ECDSA certificates can be created and used through the new extension methods.

features.title: Async output-cache providers
features.summary: ASP.NET output-cache providers can implement OutputCacheProviderAsync to read and write the cache asynchronously.

features.title: Unicode 8.0 character categories
features.summary: Characters are classified by Unicode 8.0 instead of 6.3 in CharUnicodeInfo, StringInfo, Char.GetUnicodeCategory and the regular expression engine's character classes.

features.title: RuntimeFeature capability checks
features.summary: RuntimeFeature reports whether the running runtime supports a capability such as portable PDBs.

features.title: IsReadOnlyAttribute
features.summary: IsReadOnlyAttribute is part of the framework, so compilers can mark read-only structs and in parameters.

features.title: Configuration builders
features.summary: Configuration builders let an app read parts of its configuration from external sources such as environment variables or secret stores.

features.title: HttpCookie.TryParse
features.summary: HttpCookie.TryParse parses a cookie string without throwing on bad input.

features.title: Garbage collection performance improvements
features.summary: Separate locks for small and large object heap allocations let large-object allocations proceed while background GC sweeps the small heap, reducing lock contention.

features.title: HashSet<T>.TryGetValue
features.summary: HashSet<T>.TryGetValue returns the stored element equal to a given value.

features.title: Enumerable.ToHashSet
features.summary: Enumerable.ToHashSet builds a HashSet<T> from any sequence.

features.title: RSA.Create and DSA.Create overloads
features.summary: RSA.Create and DSA.Create have overloads that take a key size or parameters.

features.title: CryptoStream leaveOpen
features.summary: A CryptoStream constructor overload can leave the underlying stream open when the CryptoStream is disposed.

features.title: Rfc2898DeriveBytes hash algorithm name
features.summary: Rfc2898DeriveBytes constructors accept a HashAlgorithmName, so PBKDF2 can use SHA-2 hashes instead of only SHA-1.

features.title: HttpClientHandler.SslProtocols and CheckCertificateRevocationList
features.summary: HttpClientHandler's SslProtocols and CheckCertificateRevocationList properties, added so the type matches .NET Standard 2.0.

netfx.note: SslProtocols and CheckCertificateRevocationList, which threw an exception when used in 4.7.1, are now implemented.

features.title: Programmatic PKCS#10 certificate requests
features.summary: Certificate signing requests (PKCS#10) can be created and processed in code.

features.title: DeflateStream decompression changes
features.summary: DeflateStream decompression uses native Windows APIs by default for apps targeting 4.7.2, which typically makes it substantially faster.

features.title: WCF service health endpoint
features.summary: A WCF service can expose a health endpoint that reports its status over HTTP.

features.title: Reduced FIPS impact on cryptography
features.summary: Managed cryptographic provider classes such as SHA256Managed no longer throw in FIPS mode; they redirect their operations to the system cryptographic libraries.

features.title: Native Arm64 support
features.summary: Native Arm64 support, so .NET Framework apps and libraries can run on Arm64 without x64 emulation.

features.title: WCAG 2.1 accessible tooltips
features.summary: Windows Forms tooltips are compliant with the WCAG 2.1 accessibility guidelines.

features.title: User-generated static_assert messages
features.summary: static_assert can take a constant expression, such as a std::string_view, as its message.

features.title: Placeholder variables with no name
features.summary: An underscore _ names a variable you do not intend to use, and it can be redeclared in the same scope.

features.title: Pack Indexing
features.summary: Ts...[N] and args...[N] select one element of a parameter pack by index.

features.title: Attributes for Structured Bindings
features.summary: Attributes can be applied to a structured binding declaration.

features.title: = delete("reason")
features.summary: = delete("reason") attaches an explanation to a deleted function that the compiler shows in the error.

features.title: Variadic friends
features.summary: A friend declaration can name a whole pack of types, as in friend Ts...;.

features.title: Structured binding declaration as a condition
features.summary: A structured binding can be declared in the condition of an if or while.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: constexpr structured bindings
features.summary: Structured bindings can be declared constexpr.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Allowing exception throwing in constant-evaluation
features.summary: Exceptions can be thrown and caught during constant evaluation.

features.title: Structured binding packs
features.summary: A structured binding can introduce a pack that holds the remaining elements, as in auto [first, ...rest] = t;.

features.title: Variadic ellipsis without comma deprecated
features.summary: Writing a variadic ellipsis without a comma, as in void f(int...), is deprecated.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Contracts
features.summary: pre(), post() and contract_assert state function preconditions, postconditions and assertions that the implementation can check.

gcc.note: Needs -fcontracts.

features.title: #embed
features.summary: #embed "file" inserts the bytes of a file as a comma-separated list of integers at compile time.

features.title: Reflection
features.summary: The ^^ operator produces a compile-time value describing a program entity, and std::meta functions inspect it, which enables code generation by introspection.

gcc.note: Needs -freflection. Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Expansion Statements
features.summary: template for iterates over the elements of a pack or tuple-like object, producing separate code for each.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: uz and z literal suffixes
features.summary: The suffixes uz and z write literals of type std::size_t and its signed counterpart, as in 10uz.

features.title: Optional () in lambdas
features.summary: The empty parameter list () is optional in every lambda, including ones with mutable or a trailing return type.

features.title: Simpler implicit move
features.summary: The rules for implicit moves from a local are simplified so a returned local can also be moved when the types differ.

features.title: if consteval
features.summary: if consteval { } else { } picks a branch depending on whether the code runs at compile time.

features.title: Deducing this
features.summary: An explicit object parameter, void f(this Self&& self), lets one member function work for any value category and replaces CRTP and duplicated overloads.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Change scope of lambda trailing-return-type
features.summary: A lambda's trailing return type can see the lambda's captured names and parameters.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Multidimensional subscript operator
features.summary: operator[] can take several arguments, as in m[i, j].

features.title: #elifdef and #elifndef
features.summary: #elifdef and #elifndef are shorthand for #elif defined(...) and #elif !defined(...).

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Alias declarations in init-statements
features.summary: The init-statement of an if, switch or for can declare a type alias.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: auto(x) decay copy
features.summary: auto(x) and auto{x} create a decayed prvalue copy of x.

features.title: Attributes on lambda expressions
features.summary: Attributes can be placed on a lambda's call operator and on the lambda expression.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Reference-binds-to-temporary type traits
features.summary: std::reference_constructs_from_temporary and std::reference_converts_from_temporary detect a reference that would bind to a temporary.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Rewritten equality comparisons fixed
features.summary: Comparison rewriting rules were fixed so reversed operator== candidates no longer cause surprising ambiguities.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: volatile compound operations un-deprecated
features.summary: Compound assignment and increment on volatile objects are no longer deprecated.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: #warning
features.summary: #warning "message" emits a diagnostic message during preprocessing and continues compiling.

features.title: Labels at the end of blocks
features.summary: A label may appear at the end of a block with nothing after it.

features.title: More relaxed constexpr
features.summary: A constexpr function may contain code that never runs at compile time, such as a call to a non-constexpr function, as long as some call can still be constant.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: static operator()
features.summary: operator() and operator[] can be static member functions.

features.title: Extended floating-point types and standard names
features.summary: std::float16_t, std::float32_t, std::float64_t, std::float128_t and std::bfloat16_t name fixed-width floating-point types when supported.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: CTAD from inherited constructors
features.summary: Class template argument deduction can use constructors inherited with using.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Portable assumptions
features.summary: [[assume(expression)]] tells the compiler an expression is true at that point so it can optimise.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: char8_t compatibility fix
features.summary: Code that relied on u8 literals being char can use them again where a char array is expected.

features.title: static constexpr variables in constexpr functions
features.summary: A constexpr function can declare a static constexpr local variable.

features.title: consteval propagates up
features.summary: A constexpr function that calls a consteval function with arguments that are not constants becomes an immediate function instead of failing to compile.

features.title: Default member initializers for bit-fields
features.summary: A bit-field member can have a default initialiser, as in int flags : 3 = 0;.

features.title: const&-qualified pointers to members
features.summary: A pointer to member function can point to a function qualified const& or const&&.

features.title: Lambda capture [=, this]
features.summary: [=, this] captures everything by value and this explicitly, since capturing this implicitly through [=] is deprecated.

features.title: __VA_OPT__
features.summary: __VA_OPT__(...) in a variadic macro expands only when variable arguments were supplied, which removes a stray comma.

features.title: Designated initializers
features.summary: An aggregate can be initialised by member name, as in Point{.x = 1, .y = 2}.

features.title: Template parameter list for lambdas
features.summary: A lambda can declare explicit template parameters, as in []<class T>(T x) { }.

features.title: Concepts
features.summary: A concept names a set of requirements on template arguments, and requires clauses use it to constrain templates.

features.title: Range-based for statements with initializer
features.summary: for (init; auto x : range) runs an initialiser before a range-based for.

features.title: Three-way comparison (operator<=>)
features.summary: operator<=> returns an ordering that the compiler uses to generate <, <=, > and >=, and = default can generate it for a class.

features.title: Lambdas in unevaluated contexts
features.summary: A lambda expression can appear in decltype, sizeof and similar unevaluated operands.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: [[no_unique_address]]
features.summary: [[no_unique_address]] lets an empty member overlap with other members instead of taking space.

features.title: [[likely]] and [[unlikely]]
features.summary: [[likely]] and [[unlikely]] hint which branch of a condition is expected to run.

features.title: typename optional in more contexts
features.summary: typename can be left out before a dependent type name in places where only a type is allowed, such as an alias or a return type.

features.title: Pack expansion in lambda init-capture
features.summary: A lambda init-capture can expand a parameter pack, as in [...args = std::move(args)].

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Class types as non-type template parameters
features.summary: A literal class type can be used as a non-type template parameter.

features.title: Generalized non-type template parameters of scalar type
features.summary: Floating-point values and other scalar types can be non-type template parameters.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Destroying operator delete
features.summary: A class can declare operator delete(T*, std::destroying_delete_t) that receives the object before destruction and performs it itself.

features.title: Relaxations of constexpr restrictions
features.summary: constexpr functions can use try blocks, virtual calls, dynamic_cast, typeid, uninitialised variables and changes of a union's active member.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Feature-test macros
features.summary: __cpp_* and __cpp_lib_* macros tell code which language and library features the compiler supports, and <version> reports the library ones.

features.title: explicit(bool)
features.summary: explicit(condition) makes a constructor or conversion operator explicit only when the compile-time condition is true.

features.title: char8_t
features.summary: char8_t is a distinct type for UTF-8 code units, and u8 string literals have that type.

features.title: consteval
features.summary: A consteval function must be evaluated at compile time, and every call to it produces a constant.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: std::is_constant_evaluated
features.summary: std::is_constant_evaluated() reports whether the enclosing code is being evaluated at compile time.

features.title: Nested inline namespaces
features.summary: namespace a::inline b { } declares a nested inline namespace in one line.

features.title: Structured binding extensions
features.summary: Names introduced by a structured binding can be captured by lambdas, and bindings can be static or thread_local.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Parenthesized initialization of aggregates
features.summary: An aggregate can be initialised with parentheses, as in Point(1, 2), which also makes std::make_unique and emplace work with aggregates.

features.title: Modules
features.summary: import replaces #include for modules, which are compiled once and export only what they declare.

gcc.note: Needs -fmodules in GCC 11 and later; modules were not usable before. Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Coroutines
features.summary: co_await, co_yield and co_return let a function suspend and resume, as the basis for generators and async tasks.

gcc.note: Needs -fcoroutines in GCC 10; on by default in -std=c++20 from GCC 11. Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: a[b, c] deprecated
features.summary: Using a comma expression inside a subscript, a[b, c], was deprecated so the syntax could later mean multiple indices.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Problematic uses of volatile deprecated
features.summary: Several uses of volatile, such as compound assignment on volatile objects, were deprecated.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: [[nodiscard("reason")]]
features.summary: [[nodiscard("reason")]] attaches an explanation that the compiler shows when the result is ignored.

features.title: using enum
features.summary: using enum E; brings an enumeration's enumerators into the current scope.

features.title: Class template argument deduction for aggregates
features.summary: Class template arguments can be deduced when initialising an aggregate, so Wrapper w{1} deduces Wrapper<int>.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Class template argument deduction for alias templates
features.summary: Class template argument deduction also works through an alias template.

gcc.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

clang.note: Documented by the vendor; no probe here confirmed this feature at this version.

features.title: Permit conversions to arrays of unknown bound
features.summary: A pointer to an array of known size converts to a pointer to an array of unknown bound.

features.title: constinit
features.summary: constinit requires a variable to be initialised at compile time while leaving it modifiable at run time.

features.title: More implicit moves
features.summary: A returned local variable or parameter is treated as an rvalue even when its own type is an rvalue reference, so it is moved instead of copied.

features.title: static_assert with no message
features.summary: static_assert can be written with only a condition, leaving out the message.

features.title: typename in a template template parameter
features.summary: A template template parameter can be introduced with typename as well as class.

features.title: Fold expressions
features.summary: A fold such as (args + ...) applies an operator across all values of a parameter pack.

features.title: u8 character literals
features.summary: u8'a' is a character literal of type char encoded as UTF-8.

features.title: Nested namespace definition
features.summary: namespace a::b::c { } declares nested namespaces in one line.

features.title: Attributes for namespaces and enumerators
features.summary: Attributes can be attached to namespaces and to individual enumerators.

features.title: Constant evaluation for all non-type template arguments
features.summary: Any constant expression, not just a restricted set, can be used as a non-type template argument.

features.title: __has_include
features.summary: __has_include(<header>) tests in a preprocessor condition whether a header can be included.

features.title: [[fallthrough]]
features.summary: [[fallthrough]] marks an intentional fall from one switch case into the next.

features.title: [[nodiscard]]
features.summary: [[nodiscard]] makes the compiler warn when a function's return value is ignored.

features.title: [[maybe_unused]]
features.summary: [[maybe_unused]] silences warnings about a declaration that may be unused.

features.title: Aggregate initialisation with base classes
features.summary: A class with public base classes can still be initialised with braces, listing the bases first.

features.title: constexpr lambda expressions
features.summary: A lambda's call operator is implicitly constexpr when it qualifies, so lambdas work in constant expressions.

features.title: Lambda capture of *this
features.summary: [*this] captures a copy of the enclosing object instead of a pointer to it.

features.title: Direct-list-initialization of enums
features.summary: An enum with a fixed underlying type can be initialised with E e{1};.

features.title: Hexadecimal floating-point literals
features.summary: 0x1.8p3 writes a floating-point literal in hexadecimal.

features.title: Using attribute namespaces without repetition
features.summary: [[using ns: a, b]] applies several attributes from one namespace without repeating the prefix.

features.title: Template argument deduction for class templates
features.summary: Class template arguments can be deduced from a constructor call, so std::pair p(1, 2.0) needs no explicit types.

features.title: Non-type template parameters with auto type
features.summary: template<auto V> accepts a non-type template argument of any type.

features.title: Guaranteed copy elision
features.summary: A prvalue initialises its destination directly, so returning or passing a temporary involves no copy or move.

features.title: constexpr if-statements
features.summary: if constexpr discards the branch that is not taken at compile time, so it need not compile for that type.

features.title: Inline variables
features.summary: inline on a variable lets its definition appear in a header without breaking the one-definition rule.

features.title: Structured bindings
features.summary: auto [a, b] = pair; unpacks a tuple-like object or struct into named variables.

features.title: if and switch with initialiser
features.summary: if (init; condition) and switch (init; value) declare a variable scoped to the statement.

features.title: Explicit conversions in array-size expressions
features.summary: The conversion used for array sizes in new expressions and similar places now also allows explicit conversion operators.

features.title: Binary literals
features.summary: 0b1010 writes an integer in binary.

features.title: decltype(auto)
features.summary: decltype(auto) deduces a type using decltype's rules, so a returned reference stays a reference.

features.title: Initialized lambda captures
features.summary: A lambda can create a new variable in its capture list, as in [p = std::move(ptr)], which also allows capturing by move.

features.title: Generic lambdas
features.summary: A lambda parameter declared auto turns the call operator into a template that accepts any argument type.

features.title: Variable templates
features.summary: A variable can be a template, such as template<class T> constexpr T pi = T(3.14159).

features.title: Member initializers and aggregates
features.summary: A class with default member initialisers can still be initialised with aggregate (braced) syntax.

features.title: [[deprecated]]
features.summary: [[deprecated]] marks a name as discouraged, so using it produces a compiler warning.

features.title: Single quotation mark as digit separator
features.summary: An apostrophe can separate digits in a numeric literal, as in 1'000'000.

features.title: Sized deallocation
features.summary: A global operator delete can receive the size of the object being freed.

features.title: Rvalue references for *this
features.summary: A member function can be qualified with & or && so it is chosen only when called on an lvalue or an rvalue object.

features.title: Non-static data member initializers
features.summary: A class member can have a default initialiser written where it is declared, used by constructors that do not set it.

features.title: Variadic templates
features.summary: Templates can take any number of type or value arguments through a parameter pack written T...

features.title: Extending variadic template template parameters
features.summary: A template template parameter can itself be variadic, so a template can accept templates with any number of parameters.

features.title: Initializer lists
features.summary: A braced list such as {1, 2, 3} can initialise containers and be received by std::initializer_list parameters.

features.title: Static assertions
features.summary: static_assert(condition, message) checks a compile-time condition and stops compilation with the message when it is false.

features.title: auto-typed variables
features.summary: auto lets the compiler deduce a variable's type from its initialiser.

features.title: Multi-declarator auto
features.summary: One auto declaration can declare several variables as long as they all deduce the same type.

features.title: Removal of auto as a storage-class specifier
features.summary: The old meaning of auto as a storage class was removed so the keyword could mean type deduction.

features.title: New function declarator syntax
features.summary: A function's return type can be written after the parameters with ->, as in auto f(int) -> int.

features.title: Lambda expressions
features.summary: An anonymous function object written [captures](params) { body } that can capture local variables.

features.title: Declared type of an expression
features.summary: decltype(expr) names the type of an expression without evaluating it.

features.title: Incomplete return types
features.summary: A function call whose return type is incomplete can be used in decltype, where no value is needed.

features.title: Right angle brackets
features.summary: Two closing angle brackets in nested templates, as in vector<vector<int>>, no longer need a space between them.

features.title: Default template arguments for function templates
features.summary: Function templates can have default template arguments, as class templates always could.

features.title: Solving the SFINAE problem for expressions
features.summary: A substitution failure inside an arbitrary expression in a signature removes the overload instead of causing an error.

features.title: Alias templates
features.summary: using Name = ...; can define a template alias, such as template<class T> using Vec = std::vector<T>.

features.title: Extern templates
features.summary: extern template tells the compiler an instantiation is provided in another translation unit, so it is not instantiated again.

features.title: Null pointer constant
features.summary: nullptr is a keyword for the null pointer with its own type, replacing the ambiguous 0 and NULL.

features.title: Strongly-typed enums
features.summary: enum class declares an enumeration whose names are scoped and which does not convert implicitly to an integer.

features.title: Forward declarations for enums
features.summary: An enum with a fixed underlying type can be declared first and defined later.

features.title: Standardized attribute syntax
features.summary: Double square brackets, as in [[noreturn]], are the standard way to attach attributes to declarations and statements.

features.title: Generalized constant expressions
features.summary: constexpr marks variables and functions that can be evaluated at compile time.

features.title: Alignment support
features.summary: alignas sets the alignment of an object or type, and alignof reports it.

features.title: Conditionally-supported behaviour
features.summary: The standard lets an implementation choose whether to support certain constructs, such as unusual pointer conversions, while requiring it to document the choice.

features.title: Delegating constructors
features.summary: A constructor can call another constructor of the same class in its initialiser list.

features.title: Inheriting constructors
features.summary: using Base::Base; makes a derived class inherit its base class's constructors.

features.title: Explicit conversion operators
features.summary: explicit on a conversion operator prevents it from being used for implicit conversions.

features.title: New character types
features.summary: char16_t and char32_t hold UTF-16 and UTF-32 code units, with u'a' and U'a' literals.

features.title: Raw string literals
features.summary: R"(text)" is a string literal in which backslashes and quotes need no escaping.

features.title: User-defined literals
features.summary: operator"" defines literal suffixes such as 5_km, so literals can create user types.

features.title: Standard Layout Types
features.summary: A standard-layout class has a predictable memory layout that matches what C expects, and std::is_standard_layout tests for it.

features.title: Defaulted functions
features.summary: = default asks the compiler to generate a special member function.

features.title: Deleted functions
features.summary: = delete makes a function unusable, so calling it is a compile error.

features.title: Extended friend declarations
features.summary: A friend declaration can name a template parameter or use a simple type name, as in friend T;.

features.title: Extending sizeof
features.summary: sizeof can be applied to a non-static data member name directly, without an object.

features.title: Inline namespaces
features.summary: A namespace declared inline makes its names visible in the enclosing namespace, which supports versioning a library's API.

features.title: Unrestricted unions
features.summary: A union can hold members with non-trivial constructors and destructors, such as std::string.

features.title: Local and unnamed types as template arguments
features.summary: Types declared inside a function, and unnamed types, can be used as template arguments.

features.title: Range-based for
features.summary: for (auto x : container) loops over every element of an array or container.

features.title: Explicit virtual overrides
features.summary: override and final state a virtual function's intent, so the compiler rejects an override that does not override anything.

features.title: Allowing move constructors to throw [noexcept]
features.summary: noexcept promises that a function does not throw, and containers use it to choose move over copy.

features.title: Defining move special member functions
features.summary: Move constructors and move assignment operators are special members that can be declared or defaulted, and the compiler generates them under defined rules.

features.title: Atomic operations
features.summary: The <atomic> header provides std::atomic types whose operations are indivisible across threads.

features.title: Memory model
features.summary: The language defines how threads see each other's memory, with std::memory_order controlling the ordering guarantees of atomic operations.

features.title: Propagating exceptions
features.summary: std::exception_ptr and std::current_exception capture an exception so it can be rethrown elsewhere, for example on another thread.

features.title: Thread-local storage
features.summary: thread_local gives each thread its own instance of a variable.

features.title: Thread-safe static initialisation
features.summary: Initialisation of function-local statics is thread-safe, so concurrent first calls initialise the variable exactly once.

features.title: __func__
features.summary: __func__ is a predefined string holding the name of the enclosing function.

features.title: C99 preprocessor
features.summary: C++ adopted C99 preprocessor features such as variadic macros (__VA_ARGS__) and empty macro arguments.

features.title: long long
features.summary: long long is a built-in integer type of at least 64 bits, with LL literals.

features.title: Relaxing requirements on constexpr functions
features.summary: constexpr functions may contain loops, local variables and multiple statements.

features.title: <array>
features.summary: std::array is a fixed-size array that knows its own size and works with the standard algorithms.

features.title: <atomic>
features.summary: std::atomic provides lock-free or locked atomic operations on a value, and the memory-order constants.

features.title: <chrono>
features.summary: A library of durations, time points and clocks with units checked at compile time.

features.title: <codecvt>
features.summary: Character-encoding conversion facets between UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 and others; deprecated in C++17.

features.title: <condition_variable>
features.summary: std::condition_variable lets a thread wait until another thread signals that a condition may have changed.

features.title: <forward_list>
features.summary: std::forward_list is a singly linked list with minimal overhead.

features.title: <future>
features.summary: std::async, std::future and std::promise pass results between threads.

features.title: <initializer_list>
features.summary: std::initializer_list is the type that receives a braced list such as {1, 2, 3}.

features.title: <mutex>
features.summary: Mutexes and locks, including std::mutex, std::lock_guard and std::unique_lock, for protecting shared data.

features.title: <random>
features.summary: Random number engines and distributions, such as std::mt19937 and std::uniform_int_distribution.

features.title: <ratio>
features.summary: std::ratio represents a compile-time rational number, used by <chrono> for time units.

features.title: <regex>
features.summary: Regular expressions with std::regex, std::regex_match and std::regex_search.

features.title: <scoped_allocator>
features.summary: std::scoped_allocator_adaptor propagates an allocator into the elements of a nested container.

features.title: <system_error>
features.summary: std::error_code, std::error_condition and std::system_error describe operating-system and library errors.

features.title: <thread>
features.summary: std::thread starts and joins operating-system threads.

features.title: <tuple>
features.summary: std::tuple holds a fixed collection of values of different types.

features.title: <typeindex>
features.summary: std::type_index wraps std::type_info so it can be used as a key in associative containers.

features.title: <type_traits>
features.summary: Compile-time queries and transformations on types, such as std::is_integral and std::remove_reference.

features.title: <unordered_map>
features.summary: std::unordered_map and std::unordered_multimap are hash tables of key-value pairs.

features.title: <unordered_set>
features.summary: std::unordered_set and std::unordered_multiset are hash tables of unique or repeated keys.

features.title: <any>
features.summary: std::any holds a single value of any copyable type and retrieves it with std::any_cast.

features.title: <execution>
features.summary: Execution policies such as std::execution::par let standard algorithms run in parallel.

features.title: <filesystem>
features.summary: std::filesystem::path and related functions inspect and manipulate files and directories.

features.title: <memory_resource>
features.summary: Polymorphic memory resources and std::pmr containers choose their allocation strategy at run time.

features.title: <optional>
features.summary: std::optional holds either a value or nothing, so a function can signal absence without a sentinel.

features.title: <shared_mutex>
features.summary: std::shared_mutex allows many readers or one writer at a time.

features.title: <string_view>
features.summary: std::string_view is a non-owning read-only view of a character sequence.

features.title: <variant>
features.summary: std::variant is a type-safe union that holds one of several listed types, visited with std::visit.

features.title: <barrier>
features.summary: std::barrier makes a group of threads wait for each other at a synchronisation point, again and again.

features.title: <bit>
features.summary: Bit manipulation helpers such as std::popcount, std::bit_cast and std::countl_zero.

features.title: <charconv>
features.summary: std::to_chars and std::from_chars convert numbers to and from text without locales or allocation.

cpp.note: The C++17 draft's header table omits <charconv>, but to_chars and from_chars are specified in the C++17 text, so C++17 is recorded.

features.title: <compare>
features.summary: The comparison category types, such as std::strong_ordering, that operator<=> returns.

features.title: <concepts>
features.summary: Standard concepts such as std::integral and std::same_as for constraining templates.

features.title: <coroutine>
features.summary: Library support for coroutines, including std::coroutine_handle and the suspend awaiters.

features.title: <format>
features.summary: std::format builds strings from a format string with typed, checked replacement fields.

features.title: <latch>
features.summary: std::latch is a single-use counter that releases waiting threads when it reaches zero.

features.title: <numbers>
features.summary: Mathematical constants such as std::numbers::pi and std::numbers::e.

features.title: <ranges>
features.summary: Range concepts, views and range-based algorithms that compose with the | operator.

features.title: <semaphore>
features.summary: std::counting_semaphore and std::binary_semaphore limit how many threads enter a section.

features.title: <source_location>
features.summary: std::source_location reports the file, line and function of the call site.

features.title: <span>
features.summary: std::span is a non-owning view of a contiguous sequence of objects.

features.title: <stop_token>
features.summary: std::stop_token and std::stop_source request cooperative cancellation of work, as used by std::jthread.

features.title: <syncstream>
features.summary: std::osyncstream collects output so that concurrent writes to one stream do not interleave.

features.title: <version>
features.summary: Including <version> defines the library feature-test macros without including anything else.

cpp.note: Specified in C++20, but GCC and Clang provide <version> in earlier modes as well.

features.title: <expected>
features.summary: std::expected holds either a value or an error, as a return type for operations that can fail.

features.title: <flat_map>
features.summary: std::flat_map and std::flat_multimap are sorted associative containers stored in contiguous arrays.

features.title: <flat_set>
features.summary: std::flat_set and std::flat_multiset are sorted set containers stored in a contiguous array.

features.title: <generator>
features.summary: std::generator is a coroutine return type that produces a lazy sequence of values.

features.title: <mdspan>
features.summary: std::mdspan is a non-owning multidimensional view over contiguous data.

features.title: <print>
features.summary: std::print and std::println write formatted text directly to a stream or stdout.

features.title: <spanstream>
features.summary: std::spanstream reads from and writes to a fixed buffer you provide, without allocating.

features.title: <stacktrace>
features.summary: std::stacktrace captures the call stack for diagnostics.

features.title: <stdfloat>
features.summary: Fixed-width floating-point types such as std::float32_t and std::bfloat16_t, where supported.

features.title: <contracts>
features.summary: Library support for contracts, such as the contract-violation handler interface.

features.title: <debugging>
features.summary: std::breakpoint and related functions that interact with a debugger.

features.title: <hazard_pointer>
features.summary: std::hazard_pointer protects objects from being reclaimed while a lock-free reader is using them.

features.title: <hive>
features.summary: std::hive is a container with stable element addresses and fast insertion and erasure anywhere.

features.title: <inplace_vector>
features.summary: std::inplace_vector is a resizable vector with fixed capacity stored inside the object, with no heap allocation.

features.title: <linalg>
features.summary: Basic linear algebra functions modelled on BLAS, working on std::mdspan arguments.

features.title: <meta>
features.summary: The std::meta functions that inspect and construct reflected program entities.

features.title: <rcu>
features.summary: Read-copy-update support, letting readers proceed without locks while writers retire old data safely.

features.title: <simd>
features.summary: std::simd types and operations for portable data-parallel arithmetic.

features.title: <text_encoding>
features.summary: std::text_encoding identifies a character encoding, such as UTF-8, by name.

features.title: Iterator-pair constructors for adaptors
features.summary: std::stack and std::queue can be constructed from an iterator pair.

features.title: constexpr std::addressof
features.summary: std::addressof can be used in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_addressof_constexpr); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: Default value type for algorithms
features.summary: Algorithms with a value parameter, such as std::ranges::find, deduce its type from the range instead of the argument.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_algorithm_default_value_type); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: Range-friendly algorithm iterator requirements
features.summary: Some algorithms, such as std::ranges::copy, accept views and iterators that were previously too restricted.

features.title: std::aligned_accessor
features.summary: A std::mdspan accessor that promises its pointer has a given alignment.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_aligned_accessor); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: allocate_at_least
features.summary: An allocator can report how many elements it actually allocated, which may be more than requested, through allocator_traits::allocate_at_least and std::allocator::allocate_at_least.

features.title: allocator_traits::is_always_equal
features.summary: A trait that tells whether all instances of an allocator are interchangeable, which lets containers skip work when moving.

features.title: std::apply
features.summary: Calls a function with the elements of a tuple as its arguments.

features.title: constexpr std::array
features.summary: More of std::array's members, such as iterators and element access, work in constant expressions.

features.title: std::as_const
features.summary: Returns a const reference to its argument.

features.title: Heterogeneous erasure
features.summary: erase and extract on ordered and unordered associative containers accept keys of another type.

features.title: Heterogeneous insertion
features.summary: insert and try_emplace on associative containers accept keys of another type.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_associative_heterogeneous_insertion); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::assume_aligned
features.summary: Tells the compiler that a pointer is aligned to a given boundary so it can generate faster code.

features.title: atomic_flag::test
features.summary: Reads a std::atomic_flag without changing it.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_atomic_flag_test); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: Atomic floating-point operations
features.summary: std::atomic<float> and std::atomic<double> support fetch_add and fetch_sub.

features.title: atomic::is_always_lock_free
features.summary: A constant that says whether an atomic type never needs a lock.

features.title: Lock-free atomic type aliases
features.summary: std::atomic_signed_lock_free and std::atomic_unsigned_lock_free name the best always-lock-free integer atomics.

gcc.note: libstdc++'s status table lists GCC 11.1; the feature-test macro is first defined here.

features.title: atomic fetch_min and fetch_max
features.summary: std::atomic gets operations that atomically store the smaller or larger of the current and a given value.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_atomic_min_max); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::atomic_ref
features.summary: Applies atomic operations to an ordinary object that already exists.

features.title: std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>
features.summary: Atomic specialisations for std::shared_ptr and std::weak_ptr, replacing the free atomic_load and atomic_store overloads.

features.title: Value-initialised atomics
features.summary: A default-constructed std::atomic is value-initialised, so it starts at zero.

features.title: Atomic wait and notify
features.summary: std::atomic can block until its value changes with wait, and wake waiters with notify_one and notify_all.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_atomic_wait); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::bind_back
features.summary: Binds the last arguments of a callable and returns a new callable for the rest.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_bind_back); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::bind_front
features.summary: Binds the first arguments of a callable and returns a new callable for the rest.

features.title: std::bit_cast
features.summary: Reinterprets the bytes of one type as another type of the same size, safely and in constant expressions.

features.title: std::bitset string_view constructor
features.summary: std::bitset can be constructed from a std::string_view.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_bitset); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::bool_constant
features.summary: An alias for std::integral_constant<bool, B>.

features.title: std::is_bounded_array and std::is_unbounded_array
features.summary: Type traits that tell whether a type is an array with a known or an unknown bound.

features.title: Boyer-Moore searchers
features.summary: std::boyer_moore_searcher and std::boyer_moore_horspool_searcher plug fast string search into std::search.

features.title: std::byte
features.summary: A type for raw memory that supports bitwise operations but not arithmetic.

features.title: std::byteswap
features.summary: Reverses the byte order of an integer.

features.title: Chrono literal suffixes
features.summary: Suffixes such as 5s, 100ms and 2h create std::chrono durations from literals.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_chrono_udls); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::clamp
features.summary: Limits a value to a range between a minimum and a maximum.

features.title: std::common_reference
features.summary: A type trait that finds a type that two reference types can both convert to.

features.title: common_reference for reference_wrapper
features.summary: std::reference_wrapper participates in std::common_reference, so it works with the ranges concepts.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_common_reference_wrapper); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: Complex literal suffixes
features.summary: The suffixes i, if and il create std::complex values from literals, as in 2.5i.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_complex_udls); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: std::constant_wrapper
features.summary: Wraps a constant expression as a type so its value can be passed through the type system.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constant_wrapper); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr algorithms
features.summary: Most of <algorithm> works in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::bitset
features.summary: std::bitset works in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr char_traits
features.summary: The character-traits functions can run at compile time, which also makes std::string_view operations constexpr.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_char_traits); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::to_chars and from_chars
features.summary: The integer overloads of std::to_chars and std::from_chars work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::complex
features.summary: std::complex operations work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::allocator
features.summary: std::allocator and std::construct_at can allocate and construct objects during constant evaluation.

features.title: constexpr exception types
features.summary: The standard exception classes can be used in constant expressions, together with constexpr exceptions in the language.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_exceptions); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::flat_map
features.summary: std::flat_map and std::flat_multimap work in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_flat_map); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::flat_set
features.summary: std::flat_set and std::flat_multiset work in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_flat_set); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::forward_list
features.summary: std::forward_list works in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_forward_list); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr <functional>
features.summary: std::invoke, the operator functors and other <functional> parts work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr iterator adaptors
features.summary: The standard iterator adaptors and iterator functions work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::list
features.summary: std::list works in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_list); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::map
features.summary: std::map and std::multimap work in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_map); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr <memory> utilities
features.summary: Functions such as std::addressof and the uninitialised-memory algorithms work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr placement new
features.summary: Placement new can be used in constant expressions.

features.summary: std::accumulate, std::iota and the other numeric algorithms work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::queue and std::stack

features.title: constexpr std::set
features.summary: std::set and std::multiset work in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_set); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr std::string
features.summary: std::string can be used in constant expressions as long as the memory is freed before evaluation ends.

features.title: constexpr std::string_view
features.summary: More of std::string_view works in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::tuple
features.summary: std::tuple works in constant expressions.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_constexpr_tuple); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: constexpr type_info comparison
features.summary: std::type_info objects can be compared in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr <utility>
features.summary: std::pair, std::swap, std::exchange and related utilities work in constant expressions.

features.title: constexpr std::vector
features.summary: std::vector can be used in constant expressions as long as the memory is freed before evaluation ends.

features.title: std::copyable_function
features.summary: A function wrapper that can hold copyable callables and supports const, noexcept and reference qualifiers.

cpp.note: Placed in this standard by the value of its feature-test macro (__cpp_lib_copyable_function); the standard's own text was not checked for this feature.

features.title: weak_from_this
features.summary: enable_shared_from_this gains weak_from_this, which returns a std::weak_ptr to the object.

features.title: std::endian
features.summary: An enumeration that tells whether the platform is little-endian or big-endian.

features.title: std::erase and std::erase_if
features.summary: Remove elements equal to a value, or matching a predicate, from a container in one call.

features.summary: Gets a pointer to the exception object held by a std::exception_ptr, without rethrowing it.

features.summary: Shuffled a range using rand() or a user function; replaced by std::shuffle with a proper random engine.

cpp.note: Deprecated because it depends on rand(); use std::shuffle.
Removed; use std::shuffle. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++17, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: register storage class
features.summary: The register keyword was an optimisation hint with no remaining effect.

cpp.note: Deprecated because compilers ignore it.
Removed; the keyword is reserved but unused. Clang 23 with libc++ and GCC 16 with libstdc++ both reject it from -std=c++17.

features.title: Trigraphs
features.summary: Three-character sequences such as ??= that stood for characters missing from some keyboards.

cpp.note: Removed from the language; the sequences keep their literal meaning. Clang 23 and GCC 16 stop replacing the sequences from -std=c++17.

features.title: Dynamic exception specifications throw(T)
features.summary: Declarations such as void f() throw(std::bad_alloc) listed the exception types a function may throw.

cpp.note: Deprecated; noexcept replaced them.
Removed; throw() was kept for one more release as an alias for noexcept(true). Clang 23 with libc++ and GCC 16 with libstdc++ both reject it from -std=c++17.

features.title: throw() specification
features.summary: void f() throw() promised that a function throws nothing; noexcept is the replacement.

cpp.note: Deprecated in favour of noexcept.
Removed; write noexcept. Clang 23 and GCC 16 still accept it at -std=c++20 (checked with -pedantic-errors).

features.title: std::result_of
features.summary: A type trait naming the result of calling a callable with given arguments; replaced by std::invoke_result.

cpp.note: Deprecated; std::invoke_result handles more callables and is easier to use.
Removed; use std::invoke_result. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++20, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: std::shared_ptr::unique
features.summary: Reported whether a shared_ptr was the only owner; not reliable under threads.

cpp.note: Deprecated because the answer can be stale in a multithreaded program.
Removed; compare use_count() with 1. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++20, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: std::uncaught_exception
features.summary: Reported whether an exception was currently propagating; replaced by std::uncaught_exceptions, which counts them.

cpp.note: Deprecated; the bool cannot handle nested unwinding.
Removed; use std::uncaught_exceptions. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++20, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: std::get_temporary_buffer
features.summary: Requested uninitialised temporary storage for algorithms; considered not useful outside the library.

cpp.note: Deprecated.
Removed. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++20, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: <cstdbool>, <ccomplex>, <ctgmath> and <ciso646>
features.summary: C++ wrappers for C headers that have no purpose in C++, such as stdbool.h.

cpp.note: Deprecated because they add nothing in C++.
Removed (<ciso646> was removed since the keywords it defined are built in). Clang 23 and GCC 16 still accept it at -std=c++20 (checked with -pedantic-errors).

features.title: <codecvt> and std::wstring_convert
features.summary: Facets that convert between UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32, and std::wstring_convert for using them.

cpp.note: Deprecated because the facets have unfixable design problems.
Removed from the standard library. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++26, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: <strstream>
features.summary: Stream classes that read and write a char array; replaced by std::stringstream and <spanstream>.

cpp.note: Listed as deprecated since the first standard because it manages raw arrays unsafely.
Removed from the standard library. Clang with libc++ rejects it from -std=c++26, but GCC's libstdc++ still accepts it for compatibility (checked with Clang 23 and GCC 16).

features.title: std::aligned_storage and std::aligned_union
features.summary: Type traits that provide properly aligned raw storage; replaced by an alignas-qualified byte array.

cpp.note: Deprecated because they are hard to use correctly and unsafe in some cases; use an alignas byte array.

features.title: std::is_pod
features.summary: Tested whether a type is both trivial and standard-layout; check the two properties separately.

cpp.note: Deprecated; use std::is_trivial and std::is_standard_layout.

features.title: std::iterator
features.summary: A helper base class that supplied the five iterator typedefs.

cpp.note: Deprecated; define the typedefs in your iterator class directly.

features.title: std::allocator<void> and allocator members such as construct
features.summary: Parts of std::allocator that the allocator_traits mechanism made unnecessary.

cpp.note: Deprecated because std::allocator_traits supplies them.
Removed. Clang 23 with libc++ and GCC 16 with libstdc++ both reject it from -std=c++20.

features.title: std::memory_order_consume
features.summary: An atomic ordering meant to follow data dependencies, which implementations treat as memory_order_acquire.

cpp.note: Deprecated because no implementation provides the intended behaviour; use memory_order_acquire.

tracks.label: ECMAScript
tracks.description: Editions of the language standard, ECMA-262. This is what the language itself defines, whichever engine runs it.

changelog_links.title: TC39 finished proposals, grouped by the edition that includes them

tracks.label: Node.js
tracks.description: Releases of the Node.js runtime. A language feature can only be used once the runtime's engine supports it, so this track records the first Node.js release that runs each one, plus APIs that exist only in Node.js.

changelog_links.title: Node.js release schedule: release dates, long-term support and end of life
Node.js API documentation, with a history table for each API
MDN browser compatibility data, the source for engine feature support

tracks.label: Python
tracks.description: Versions of the Python language and its standard library. Python 2 is recorded as a single baseline, so the page can show what changed for code moving from Python 2 to Python 3 and between 3.x releases.

changelog_links.title: What's New in Python, one page per version
Status of Python versions, with release and end-of-life dates

tracks.label: Rust
tracks.description: Releases of the Rust compiler and standard library, listed only where a release introduced something this reference tracks. If your toolchain is not listed, use the nearest earlier release: a feature stays available in later releases unless it is marked removed.

changelog_links.title: Release notes for every Rust release
Rust blog, with a post for each release

tracks.label: Rust editions
tracks.description: Rust's editions (2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024) are opt-in sets of language rules that each crate chooses for itself. They change how code is parsed and how a few features behave, and crates on different editions work together. This track shows what changes when you move a crate to a newer edition.

tracks.label: C# language versions
tracks.description: Versions of the C# language, from 1.0 to 14. Each C# version needs a compiler that understands it and, for some features, a runtime that supports it; the compiler's default version depends on the target framework (.NET 10 uses C# 14, .NET 8 uses C# 12, .NET Framework uses 7.3). Features that depend on runtime support say which runtimes accept them.

tracks.label: .NET (Core and 5+)
tracks.description: Releases of modern .NET: .NET Core 1.0 to 3.1, then .NET 5 to 10. Listed only where a release introduced something this reference tracks, so if your release is missing use the nearest earlier one. Each release shows its default C# version, long-term-support status and end-of-support date from the .NET release feed.

tracks.label: .NET Framework
tracks.description: Releases of the Windows-only .NET Framework, 4.5 to 4.8.1. Its compiler default is C# 7.3, and several newer C# features do not compile against its reference assemblies (for example default interface members, static abstract members, ref fields, records, ranges and async streams). The release date shown is the start of Microsoft's support lifecycle for that release.

tracks.label: C++ standards
tracks.description: The ISO C++ standards from C++98, the canonical language timeline. Each entry says which standard first specified a feature, and the lifecycle entries trace what was deprecated and then removed. C++26 is technically complete but ISO had not published it when this was written, so it is listed as a draft. The publication months of the ISO standards are from general knowledge; the ISO catalogue was not read for this.

changelog_links.title: C++ working draft (source of the standard's text)

tracks.label: GCC
tracks.description: GCC releases and the C++ support each one added, together with libstdc++ of the same version. Versions 9 to 16 are marked verified: each was run here with its own libstdc++. Older versions and the events that come from the vendor's documentation are marked as not verified. GCC 17 is in development and is not listed.

tracks.label: Clang
tracks.description: Clang releases and the C++ support each one added, with libc++ of the same version for library features. Versions 14 to 23 are marked verified: each was run here with its own libc++. Older versions come from the vendor's documentation and are marked as not verified. Clang 24 is unreleased and is not listed.

tracks.label: MSVC
tracks.description: Microsoft's C++ compiler as shipped in Visual Studio, with the MSVC standard library. MSVC cannot be run on this platform, so none of its versions is marked verified; every entry comes from Microsoft's conformance table. Release dates are Visual Studio release dates.
